## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

## omnifocus
OmniFocus is a GTD task manager. Hierarchy: Folders > Projects > Tasks > Subtasks.

TASK STATES: Available, Blocked, Deferred (future defer date), Flagged, Overdue, Completed, Dropped. Planned Date is a scheduling signal only — no availability/overdue constraints.

PROJECT TYPES: "sequential" (tasks in order; first incomplete = available, rest blocked; position = dependencies), "parallel" (all available), "single_actions" (no completion goal, cannot auto-complete). The `next` field is true for the first available action in a sequential project/action group; in parallel projects, all incomplete tasks have `next: true`.

ACTION GROUPS: Task with subtasks. Parent shows `blocked: true` while subtasks are active — this is normal, not an error. Do not try to unblock it.

INHERITED STATUS: `completed`/`dropped` reflect the task's own state, not its container's. `effectivelyCompleted`/`effectivelyDropped` reflect the container's state — if true, the task's parent project or action group was completed/dropped. Task in completed project: `completed: false`, `effectivelyCompleted: true`, `available: false`. Use `available_only=True` for actionable tasks.

EFFECTIVE DATES: Dates returned by get_tasks are always effective (inherited). A task with no direct due date WILL show its project's due date in the dueDate field — this is correct behavior, not a bug. You cannot clear an inherited date at the task level. Write operations set the task's own date.

RECURRING TASKS: `completed=True` uses `mark complete`, which creates the next occurrence. This is guaranteed. WARNING: Dropping a recurring task (status='dropped') without clearing recurrence first (recurrence='') spawns the next occurrence. To stop a series: update_tasks([{"id": "...", "recurrence": "", "status": "dropped"}]).

TAGS: Represent work contexts. Tag statuses: Active (normal), On Hold (tasks excluded from Available perspective), Dropped (tag hidden from picker; does NOT affect task availability).

DEFER vs DUE: Defer = hidden until that date. Due = deadline.

1	# Spending Report Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-09
4	**Status:** 🚧 **Mostly built.** Every slice described below is live except the
5	six listed under _Left_.
6	
7	**Live:** the table view, the chart view, table-cell drill-down into Expenses,
8	the editable hierarchy (assign a Category to a Grouping, re-parent a Grouping,
9	add & rename Groupings), assign-on-create, historical-year expense import from
10	CSV/Excel, and year-over-year comparison (a Change column on the table +
11	side-by-side prior-year bars on the chart).
12	
13	**Left**, roughly in order of value:
14	
15	- **Chart-bar drill-down** — table cells link into `/expenses`; chart bars still
16	  don't. `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` already exists, so this is wiring.
17	- **Cumulative pace line** and **diverging change bars** — the two richer YoY
18	  views ([options 3 and 4](#the-options-cheapest--richest)). Diverging bars are
19	  also the only remaining way to surface _disappeared_ spend.
20	- **Quarter / arbitrary period selection**, and a **multi-chart-type menu**.
21	- **Export** (CSV / PDF), and **promoting the report to the home page**.
22	
23	Plus one small live defect: the **"Year to Date"** column heading is hardcoded,
24	so it now reads wrong for an imported past year (see
25	[Known limitations](#known-limitations-document-when-building)).
26	
27	**Will not be built** — settled, not deferred: **Importance-area CRUD** (the 3
28	areas are fixed); **Grouping delete and reorder**; and the **Bridge / waterfall**
29	view, which was built and then **removed as not intuitive**
30	([ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) — do not
31	rebuild it).
32	
33	## Overview
34	
35	A top-level **Spending** report that rolls up Expenses by **Importance →
36	Grouping → Category** across the months of a year. It replaces the Excel pivot
37	table the family currently maintains by hand. ("Spending Report" is the working
38	term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)
39	
40	Built ✅: the **table view** (v1), the **chart view** (an accordion magnitude bar
41	chart), **cell drill-down** into the Expenses view, and **hierarchy editing**
42	(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, assign-on-create) — see
43	[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
44	[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),
45	[Drill-down](#drill-from-a-table-cell-into-the-expenses-view--built-), and
46	[Editable hierarchy](#editable-hierarchy--assign--re-parent--built-). Year-over-year
47	comparison (a table Change column + chart marker) is also built (see
48	[Year-over-year comparison](#year-over-year-comparison--table-columns--bar-marker-built-)).
49	Still deferred: selectable periods, richer YoY views (pace line / diverging),
50	tier CRUD, and export (see [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices)).
51	
52	## Data model (new)
53	
54	The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
55	There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
56	family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.
57	
58	- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
59	  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
60	  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
61	- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
62	  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
63	  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
64	  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
65	  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
66	- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
67	  Group; the Group carries the Importance.
68	
69	**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
70	`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
71	Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
72	`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
73	auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
74	New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
75	future family gets a working report out of the box.
76	
77	## Report content
78	
79	- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
80	  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
81	  date).
82	- **Currency:** normalized to the family's display currency —
83	  `total_amount × (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`. CAD for now; the assumption is
84	  isolated so multi-currency drops in later.
85	- **Columns:** January → the last month that has any expense (left edge stays at
86	  January for a stable calendar grid). Interior/empty cells render blank, not
87	  `$0.00`. Final column is labelled **"Year to Date."**
88	- **Rows:** four row types — category detail, **Grouping subtotal**,
89	  **Importance subtotal**, and a final **Grand Total**. Importance ordered by
90	  `sort_order` (Essential → Priorities → Other); Groupings alphabetical within an
91	  Importance; Categories alphabetical within a Grouping. **Zero-activity rows are
92	  suppressed** (a category/group with no spend in the visible window is hidden).
93	- **Uncategorized:** rendered as its own section at the bottom, outside the real
94	  Importance/Grouping subtotals. It **is included in the Grand Total** (and any
95	  month-column totals), so the bottom-right number ties out to the family's
96	  actual total spend. The gap between the three Importance subtotals and the
97	  Grand Total is the deliberate nudge to go categorize.
98	- **Null amounts:** counted as `$0`. No new flag — the receipts and expenses
99	  pages already badge these (`⚠ Amount not read`). At most a small "N receipts
100	  missing an amount" footnote deep-linking to that existing filtered view.
101	
102	## Architecture
103	
104	- **Client-side pure aggregation.** A tested pure function
105	  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, hierarchy, year) → grid`, in the style of the
106	  CSV parsers and date utilities. The small hierarchy tables and the year's
107	  expenses are fetched separately and joined in TypeScript — the existing
108	  expense query is not widened. A family's yearly receipt count is small, so the
109	  data transfer is negligible and the logic stays unit-testable. If volume ever
110	  demands it, swap in a Postgres RPC behind the same function boundary — this
111	  avoids the RLS-fragility minefield the codebase repeatedly warns about.
112	- **Placement:** a new top-level **`/spending`** tab, following the existing
113	  `resolve()` / `filterQuery` nav pattern. May be promoted to the home page
114	  later once proven (currently `/` is "Family Receipts") — a separate change.
115	- **No editing UI in v1.** The hierarchy is hand-maintained (direct SQL) while
116	  the family is a single maintainer. The Uncategorized bucket is the feedback
117	  loop for anything unmapped.
118	
119	## Implementation status ✅
120	
121	v1 is built and running against live data (v0.50). What landed:
122	
123	- **Migration** `supabase/migrations/20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql` — creates
124	  `importance_areas` and `category_groups`, adds `categories.group_id`
125	  (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), family-scoped RLS mirroring `categories_family_access`,
126	  unique-per-family name indexes, and `updated_at` triggers. Ships
127	  `create_default_hierarchy(p_family_id)` (idempotent, `SECURITY DEFINER`): seeds
128	  3 Importance areas + 13 Groupings and maps categories → groups by name (a
129	  superset covering both the current default names and the older spreadsheet
130	  names). Backfills every existing family in a `DO` loop; the app calls it via
131	  RPC for new families.
132	- **Grouping → Importance seed choices.** Each Grouping is collapsed to a single
133	  Importance (the model attaches Importance to the Grouping): **Essential** =
134	  Everyday, Health, Home, Transportation, Income Taxes; **Priorities** = Banking
135	  & Investing, Debt, Fitness, Kids, Rental; **Other** = Discretionary, Gifts,
136	  Travel. Where the source spreadsheet split a Grouping across importances (e.g.
137	  Home's Garden/Household goods were "Other"), it now rolls up under the
138	  Grouping's single Importance. Change with a one-row `UPDATE` on
139	  `category_groups.importance_area_id`.
140	- **Aggregation** `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts` — the pure
141	  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, categories, groups, importanceAreas, year)`.
142	  21 unit tests in `spendingReport.spec.ts` (month columns, roll-up/subtotals,
143	  ordering, Uncategorized, refund netting, FX, null amounts, blank-vs-zero cells).
144	  Per-cell `{ amount, count }` drives blank (count 0) vs `0.00` (net-zero but had
145	  activity).
146	- **Types** `src/lib/types/Hierarchy.ts` (`ImportanceArea`, `CategoryGroup`);
147	  `Category` gains `group_id`.
148	- **Service** `CategoryService` gains `getFamilyImportanceAreas`,
149	  `getFamilyGroups`, and `createDefaultHierarchy` (RPC wrapper).
150	- **Page + nav** `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte` + a **Spending** top-level
151	  tab. Self-seeds the hierarchy on first open (mirrors default-categories
152	  lazy-init), then loads hierarchy + the year's expenses and paints the grid.
153	  Year prev/next selector, missing-amount footnote, Importance bands, Grouping
154	  and Importance subtotals, Uncategorized section, Grand Total. The **selected
155	  year lives in the URL** (`/spending?year=2025`) and is read in a **`+page.ts`
156	  `load`** (pure `parseYearParam`); the page consumes `data.year`, and the year
157	  arrows `goto('?year=…', { replaceState: true })`. A reload `$effect` fires when
158	  `data.year` (or the resolved family) changes. `load` is the single source of
159	  truth: SvelteKit re-runs it with the correct URL on every navigation — arrows,
160	  a refresh, and **Back from a cell drill-down** — so it never snaps back to the
161	  current year (which would show an empty grid for a data-only-in-2025 family).
162	  Three client-side attempts failed first and are recorded so they aren't retried:
163	  (1) read-once-in-`onMount` raced the initial render; (2) `$derived` off the
164	  legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store went stale on Back; (3) `$derived` off the
165	  `$app/state` reactive `page` _plus_ `replaceState`-driven arrows still went
166	  stale on Back and left the arrows inert. The `load` approach is the robust fix.
167	- **Rendering details.** Long category names truncate to one line
168	  (`max-w-64 truncate`) with the full name on hover via `title`. The layout gives
169	  `/spending` full window width (`max-w-full`); other pages keep `max-w-5xl`.
170	
171	**Verification:** `npm run check`, `eslint`, and Prettier clean on touched files;
172	full unit suite green (1278 passed / 8 skipped, incl. the 21 new). Production
173	build succeeds. Not yet exercised: a rendered end-to-end pass (no local
174	auth/seed harness) — validated live by the maintainer instead.
175	
176	**Known open item surfaced by live data:** the seed maps by name, so any custom
177	or renamed category lands in Uncategorized until its `group_id` is set by hand.
178

409	## Year-over-year comparison — table columns & bar marker built ✅
410	
411	Now that historical years can be uploaded, the report can show **how spending
412	changed vs. prior years**. This section catalogues the visualization options,
413	then records what shipped first.
414	
415	### The parity rule (load-bearing — governs every option)
416	
417	Every comparison shares one primitive: a **period cutoff** derived from the
418	selected year's own data, applied identically to each comparison year.
419	
420	- **Cutoff = the selected year's last visible month** — the same `maxMonth` the
421	  report already computes for the rightmost ("Year to Date") column. Reused, not
422	  re-derived.
423	- Each comparison year is summed **January → cutoff month only**. A partial 2026
424	  (Jan–Jul) is compared against **Jan–Jul** of the prior year, never its full
425	  Jan–Dec — so a half-finished current year can't lose by construction.
426	- **Whole months only** (the shipped choice). Today being 2026-07-10, July is
427	  partial in 2026 but was complete in 2025; the month-boundary rule compares
428	  Jan–Jul wholesale rather than clipping both to Jul 10. Simpler, matches the
429	  monthly grid, and is what the maintainer asked to start with. A day-boundary
430	  "pace" comparison is possible later (see the cumulative line below) but is not
431	  built.
432	
433	### The options (cheapest → richest)
434	
435	1. **YoY table column** — after "Year to Date", a single **Change** column
436	   (Δ amount + % vs the same Jan→cutoff period last year). Same roll-up levels as
437	   today (category / group / importance / grand total). Pure extension of the
438	   aggregate; no new chart infra. **Built (below)** — a separate Prior-YTD column
439	   was prototyped but dropped as redundant (the change alone carries the signal;
440	   the prior total remains one hover away in the chart tooltip).
441	2. **Prior-period marker on the magnitude bars** — a horizontal tick / ghost line
442	   at each bar's prior-YTD value; the gap between bar top and tick _is_ the
443	   change, read in place with the accordion still working. **Built (below).**
444	3. **Cumulative "pace" line chart** — x = month (Jan → cutoff), y = running
445	   cumulative spend, **one line per year** overlaid, every line stopping at the
446	   same cutoff x so the parity rule is visually self-evident. The natural home
447	   for the month/time story deliberately dropped off the bars. **Deferred.**
448	4. **Diverging change bars** — one bar per Grouping = Δ vs prior YTD, increases
449	   one way / decreases the other, sorted by magnitude; best for _what_ changed.
450	   **Deferred.** (Colour caution: the app already binds red = expense /
451	   green = refund, so a diverging chart must not reuse red/green for
452	   direction — use a neutral diverging pair or encode direction by side + sign.)
453	5. **Waterfall / bridge** — prior-YTD total → one ±step per Grouping →
454	   current-YTD total; decomposes the entire YoY change. Richest, least reuse.
455	   **Built as a horizontal bridge, then ABANDONED as not intuitive** — see
456	   [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md). Do not
457	   rebuild it; if "what changed, ranked" is wanted, prefer option 4.
458	
459	Deliberately skipped: month×grouping heatmaps and indexed-to-100 growth curves —
460	legible only to spreadsheet-native users, and this report exists to _replace_ the
461	family's manual pivot, not re-create its density.
462	
463	### What shipped (options 1 + 2; option 5 abandoned)
464	
465	- **Toggle.** A **`Compare {priorYear}`** button in the header (next to
466	  Table | Chart) turns the comparison on/off for **both** views. When the prior
467	  year has **no data**, the toggle still renders but is **disabled** with an
468	  explanatory `title` ("No {priorYear} data to compare"). Effective state is
469	  `comparing = compare && hasPrior`, so stepping the year selector onto a year
470	  whose predecessor has no data silently disables it and re-enables on return.
471	  Comparison is **local page state** (like the Table | Chart toggle), not URL —
472	  it doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.
473	- **Pure core.** `withPriorPeriod(report, priorReport)` in
474	  `src/lib/utils/spendingComparison.ts` attaches `priorYtd` (optional field added
475	  to `ReportRow`) to every row/subtotal/grand-total by summing the prior report's
476	  cells over the first `report.months.length` months (the parity window), matched
477	  by **id** (categoryId / groupId / importanceId) with `(No category)` matched by
478	  name. `spendingChange(current, prior) → { delta, pct, direction }` computes the
479	  Change cell (pct is `null` when prior is 0 → rendered "new"); `hasPriorData`
480	  gates the toggle. Both are unit-tested (`spendingComparison.spec.ts`).
481	- **Table.** A single **Change** column folds into the existing `valueCells`
482	  snippet so every row type gets it; it shows a signed amount + % coloured by
483	  direction (increase / decrease / flat) — no user-facing legend copy. The
484	  Importance/Uncategorized band `colspan`s widen by 1 when comparing. (The
485	  Prior-YTD column was dropped as redundant — see option 1.)
486	- **Chart.** `buildSpendingChart` carries `priorTotal` onto each `ChartBar`
487	  (from the group/category `priorYtd`); `SpendingChart` (new `compare` prop) shows
488	  a **faded prior-year bar side by side** with each current-year bar, and adds the
489	  prior total + change to the hover tooltip. (The bars are drawn as scale-derived
490	  overlays and LayerChart's own bars hidden via `props.bars.opacity`, so current
491	  and prior can sit side by side; the y-domain is sized to the taller of the two
492	  years. Superseded the first cut — a dashed prior-period line — which read as an
493	  ambiguous threshold.) Data loading fetches the prior year's expenses alongside
494	  the current year's (volume is negligible per the aggregate's own design note),
495	  so switching the toggle repaints instantly with no refetch.
496	- **Bridge (option 5) — built, then ABANDONED.** ⚠️ This view was built and pulled
497	  because **users didn't understand it intuitively** — see
498	  [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) and the
499	  reminder screenshot [`docs/BridgeChartTooWide.png`](../BridgeChartTooWide.png).
500	  The description below is kept as a record of what was tried; the code
501	  (`SpendingBridge.svelte`, `spendingWaterfall.ts`, their specs, and the `Bridge`
502	  toggle) has been **removed**. **Do not rebuild it.** A **horizontal waterfall**
503	  with the **areas on the Y-axis** and the running cumulative amount on the
504	  X-axis: the top anchor is the prior-year same-period grand total, one floating
505	  step per area (up = spent more / down = spent less, same red/green as the Change
506	  column), the bottom anchor is the current-year grand total — the steps always
507	  reconcile.
508	  - **Pure core** `buildWaterfallBridge(current, prior, expandedGroups)` in
509	    `src/lib/utils/spendingWaterfall.ts`. Unlike the magnitude chart it reads
510	    **both** reports and walks the **union** of groups/categories across the two
511	    years, so a **disappeared** area (spent last year, nothing this year — no
512	    current row) still appears as its own downward step. Prior totals use the same
513	    whole-month parity window. Reconciliation holds at every level: Σ step deltas =
514	    current − prior grand total. 10 unit tests (`spendingWaterfall.spec.ts`).
515	  - **Accordion preserved.** Expanding a Grouping emits a **header row** (which
516	    keeps the − collapse toggle and shows the group's net change at 40 % opacity)

518	    group delta, the running total on either side is unchanged. Many open at once
519	    (`SvelteSet`), like the magnitude chart.
520	  - **Rendering** is a self-contained `SpendingBridge.svelte` — percentage-scaled
521	    off the model's running-total domain (no width measurement, resizes for free),
522	    Importance colour on the row's left border + a legend, hover tooltip with
523	    current / prior / change. Only reachable when the prior year has data (the
524	    `Bridge` toggle is disabled otherwise). 3 render tests.

557	## Known limitations (document when building)
558	
559	- **Refunds.** Refunds are represented as **negative `total_amount`** on a
560	  receipt (confirmed via `formatCurrency.spec.ts` and the export services). The
561	  report **keeps the sign**, so refunds net against spend — which is the correct
562	  behaviour for a spending total. (Note the CSV/PDF _exporters_ deliberately
563	  `abs()` refunds; the report does not.) One visible consequence: a Category or
564	  Grouping whose refunds exceed its spend in the window shows a **negative**

567	- **"Year to Date" label** reads oddly for a _completed past_ year (it is the
568	  full-year total). This was written off as "not a v1 problem since v1 is
569	  current-year only" — **that premise expired** when historical-year import
570	  shipped, so a family that has imported 2024 now sees "Year to Date" over a

# Spending Report Design

**Date:** 2026-07-09
**Status:** 🚧 **Mostly built.** Every slice described below is live except the
six listed under _Left_.

**Live:** the table view, the chart view, table-cell drill-down into Expenses,
the editable hierarchy (assign a Category to a Grouping, re-parent a Grouping,
add & rename Groupings), assign-on-create, historical-year expense import from
CSV/Excel, and year-over-year comparison (a Change column on the table +
side-by-side prior-year bars on the chart).

**Left**, roughly in order of value:

- **Chart-bar drill-down** — table cells link into `/expenses`; chart bars still
  don't. `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` already exists, so this is wiring.
- **Cumulative pace line** and **diverging change bars** — the two richer YoY
  views ([options 3 and 4](#the-options-cheapest--richest)). Diverging bars are
  also the only remaining way to surface _disappeared_ spend.
- **Quarter / arbitrary period selection**, and a **multi-chart-type menu**.
- **Export** (CSV / PDF), and **promoting the report to the home page**.

Plus one small live defect: the **"Year to Date"** column heading is hardcoded,
so it now reads wrong for an imported past year (see
[Known limitations](#known-limitations-document-when-building)).

**Will not be built** — settled, not deferred: **Importance-area CRUD** (the 3
areas are fixed); **Grouping delete and reorder**; and the **Bridge / waterfall**
view, which was built and then **removed as not intuitive**
([ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) — do not
rebuild it).

## Overview

A top-level **Spending** report that rolls up Expenses by **Importance →
Grouping → Category** across the months of a year. It replaces the Excel pivot
table the family currently maintains by hand. ("Spending Report" is the working
term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)

Built ✅: the **table view** (v1), the **chart view** (an accordion magnitude bar
chart), **cell drill-down** into the Expenses view, and **hierarchy editing**
(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, assign-on-create) — see
[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),
[Drill-down](#drill-from-a-table-cell-into-the-expenses-view--built-), and
[Editable hierarchy](#editable-hierarchy--assign--re-parent--built-). Year-over-year
comparison (a table Change column + chart marker) is also built (see
[Year-over-year comparison](#year-over-year-comparison--table-columns--bar-marker-built-)).
Still deferred: selectable periods, richer YoY views (pace line / diverging),
tier CRUD, and export (see [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices)).

## Data model (new)

The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.

- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
  Group; the Group carries the Importance.

**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
future family gets a working report out of the box.

## Report content

- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
  date).
- **Currency:** normalized to the family's display currency —
  `total_amount × (exchange_rate_to_cad ?? 1)`. CAD for now; the assumption is
  isolated so multi-currency drops in later.
- **Columns:** January → the last month that has any expense (left edge stays at
  January for a stable calendar grid). Interior/empty cells render blank, not
  `$0.00`. Final column is labelled **"Year to Date."**
- **Rows:** four row types — category detail, **Grouping subtotal**,
  **Importance subtotal**, and a final **Grand Total**. Importance ordered by
  `sort_order` (Essential → Priorities → Other); Groupings alphabetical within an
  Importance; Categories alphabetical within a Grouping. **Zero-activity rows are
  suppressed** (a category/group with no spend in the visible window is hidden).
- **Uncategorized:** rendered as its own section at the bottom, outside the real
  Importance/Grouping subtotals. It **is included in the Grand Total** (and any
  month-column totals), so the bottom-right number ties out to the family's
  actual total spend. The gap between the three Importance subtotals and the
  Grand Total is the deliberate nudge to go categorize.
- **Null amounts:** counted as `$0`. No new flag — the receipts and expenses
  pages already badge these (`⚠ Amount not read`). At most a small "N receipts
  missing an amount" footnote deep-linking to that existing filtered view.

## Architecture

- **Client-side pure aggregation.** A tested pure function
  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, hierarchy, year) → grid`, in the style of the
  CSV parsers and date utilities. The small hierarchy tables and the year's
  expenses are fetched separately and joined in TypeScript — the existing
  expense query is not widened. A family's yearly receipt count is small, so the
  data transfer is negligible and the logic stays unit-testable. If volume ever
  demands it, swap in a Postgres RPC behind the same function boundary — this
  avoids the RLS-fragility minefield the codebase repeatedly warns about.
- **Placement:** a new top-level **`/spending`** tab, following the existing
  `resolve()` / `filterQuery` nav pattern. May be promoted to the home page
  later once proven (currently `/` is "Family Receipts") — a separate change.
- **No editing UI in v1.** The hierarchy is hand-maintained (direct SQL) while
  the family is a single maintainer. The Uncategorized bucket is the feedback
  loop for anything unmapped.

## Implementation status ✅

v1 is built and running against live data (v0.50). What landed:

- **Migration** `supabase/migrations/20260709_spending_hierarchy.sql` — creates
  `importance_areas` and `category_groups`, adds `categories.group_id`
  (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), family-scoped RLS mirroring `categories_family_access`,
  unique-per-family name indexes, and `updated_at` triggers. Ships
  `create_default_hierarchy(p_family_id)` (idempotent, `SECURITY DEFINER`): seeds
  3 Importance areas + 13 Groupings and maps categories → groups by name (a
  superset covering both the current default names and the older spreadsheet
  names). Backfills every existing family in a `DO` loop; the app calls it via
  RPC for new families.
- **Grouping → Importance seed choices.** Each Grouping is collapsed to a single
  Importance (the model attaches Importance to the Grouping): **Essential** =
  Everyday, Health, Home, Transportation, Income Taxes; **Priorities** = Banking
  & Investing, Debt, Fitness, Kids, Rental; **Other** = Discretionary, Gifts,
  Travel. Where the source spreadsheet split a Grouping across importances (e.g.
  Home's Garden/Household goods were "Other"), it now rolls up under the
  Grouping's single Importance. Change with a one-row `UPDATE` on
  `category_groups.importance_area_id`.
- **Aggregation** `src/lib/utils/spendingReport.ts` — the pure
  `buildSpendingReport(expenses, categories, groups, importanceAreas, year)`.
  21 unit tests in `spendingReport.spec.ts` (month columns, roll-up/subtotals,
  ordering, Uncategorized, refund netting, FX, null amounts, blank-vs-zero cells).
  Per-cell `{ amount, count }` drives blank (count 0) vs `0.00` (net-zero but had
  activity).
- **Types** `src/lib/types/Hierarchy.ts` (`ImportanceArea`, `CategoryGroup`);
  `Category` gains `group_id`.
- **Service** `CategoryService` gains `getFamilyImportanceAreas`,
  `getFamilyGroups`, and `createDefaultHierarchy` (RPC wrapper).
- **Page + nav** `src/routes/spending/+page.svelte` + a **Spending** top-level
  tab. Self-seeds the hierarchy on first open (mirrors default-categories
  lazy-init), then loads hierarchy + the year's expenses and paints the grid.
  Year prev/next selector, missing-amount footnote, Importance bands, Grouping
  and Importance subtotals, Uncategorized section, Grand Total. The **selected
  year lives in the URL** (`/spending?year=2025`) and is read in a **`+page.ts`
  `load`** (pure `parseYearParam`); the page consumes `data.year`, and the year
  arrows `goto('?year=…', { replaceState: true })`. A reload `$effect` fires when
  `data.year` (or the resolved family) changes. `load` is the single source of
  truth: SvelteKit re-runs it with the correct URL on every navigation — arrows,
  a refresh, and **Back from a cell drill-down** — so it never snaps back to the
  current year (which would show an empty grid for a data-only-in-2025 family).
  Three client-side attempts failed first and are recorded so they aren't retried:
  (1) read-once-in-`onMount` raced the initial render; (2) `$derived` off the
  legacy `$app/stores` `$page` store went stale on Back; (3) `$derived` off the
  `$app/state` reactive `page` _plus_ `replaceState`-driven arrows still went
  stale on Back and left the arrows inert. The `load` approach is the robust fix.
- **Rendering details.** Long category names truncate to one line
  (`max-w-64 truncate`) with the full name on hover via `title`. The layout gives
  `/spending` full window width (`max-w-full`); other pages keep `max-w-5xl`.

**Verification:** `npm run check`, `eslint`, and Prettier clean on touched files;
full unit suite green (1278 passed / 8 skipped, incl. the 21 new). Production
build succeeds. Not yet exercised: a rendered end-to-end pass (no local
auth/seed harness) — validated live by the maintainer instead.

**Known open item surfaced by live data:** the seed maps by name, so any custom
or renamed category lands in Uncategorized until its `group_id` is set by hand.

## Spending Chart (graphical presentation) — built ✅

A `Table | Chart` toggle on `/spending` (shared year selector + loaded data)
adds a **magnitude bar chart** view (v0.60).

> **Design note — why not stacked-by-month.** The first cut stacked 12 month
> segments per bar with a sequential ramp. In real data it failed twice: the 12
> subtle shades read as noise ("the gradient is a mess"), and one dominant
> Grouping (a family's ~$33k Home, driven by a one-off $20k renovation) crushed
> every other bar's height so small bars were unreadable. Both flaws trace to the
> month stack. v0.60 drops it: **solid magnitude bars + value labels**, with the
> month/time story deferred to the separate trend chart.

- **Form:** one **solid bar per Grouping** = its year-to-date total, **coloured by
  Area of Importance** (a validated 3-colour categorical palette: Essential
  `#4f46e5`, Priorities `#0d9488`, Other `#d97706`; Uncategorized neutral gray).
  Bars ordered by Importance `sort_order` then Grouping name; **Uncategorized**
  trails; zero-activity groups suppressed.
- **Value label** above every bar (formatted currency), so a tiny bar next to a
  dominant one is still readable — the fix for the outlier problem without a
  scale hack. Positioned from the bound LayerChart `context` (band x-scale +
  linear y-scale).
- **Two bracket rows beneath the axis** carry the hierarchy, both positioned from
  the bound `context` band x-scale (aligned on resize):
  - **Row 1 — Grouping ± toggles.** One keyboard-focusable `<button>` bracket per
    Grouping, spanning its bar(s), showing `+ Name` / `− Name`. This is the
    expand/collapse control (see interaction) and the Grouping label.
  - **Row 2 — Area of Importance**, labelled **once per contiguous run** of
    same-Importance bars, in that Importance's colour. Uncategorized has no
    Importance bracket (its Grouping bracket names it).
- **Interaction: expand in place (accordion), not drill-and-replace.** Clicking a
  Grouping's bar **or** its ± bracket expands it into its **Category** bars _in
  place_ while its siblings stay visible; **any number of Groupings can be open at
  once** (`expandedGroups` is a reactive `SvelteSet`). Expanded Categories keep the
  parent Grouping's Importance colour and sit inside the same Importance bracket.
  Bars are keyed by a unique id, not name, so same-named Categories across
  Groupings don't collide on the band scale.
- **Click + hover come from a custom per-bar overlay, not LayerChart.** LayerChart's
  own tooltip layer both swallows bar clicks and can't carry a month breakdown, so
  `tooltipContext` is disabled and a transparent full-height column is drawn over
  each bar (from the band scale). It handles the click (toggle its Grouping) and the
  hover, which shows a **tooltip with the bar's name, its per-month totals, and the
  grand total** — the monthly detail dropped from the bars themselves. The overlay
  columns are `aria-hidden`/non-focusable mouse affordances; the ± brackets remain
  the keyboard-accessible controls.
- **Long labels don't collide.** When a Grouping expands into many Category bars,
  each axis label is truncated to one bar width with an ellipsis (`Meals and Drinks
Out` → `Meals…`); the full name is in the hover tooltip. Collapsed Grouping names
  live in their ± bracket (truncated there too). The one-line usage hint sits below
  the chart.
- **Data:** no new aggregation — the pure
  `buildSpendingChart(report, expandedGroups)` reshapes the existing
  `SpendingReport` into a flat `{ months, bars }` where expanded Groupings
  contribute their Category bars in place (unit-tested in `spendingChart.spec.ts`).
  The per-bar `monthly` map is retained for the future trend chart / hover detail;
  the current view uses only `total`.
- **Library:** **LayerChart 2.0.1** (`<BarChart>` with `y="total"` and a `c`
  ordinal colour scale by Importance; `bandPadding`, rounded bars). Peer
  `svelte@^5`. Its built-in tooltip/click layer (`tooltipContext`) is **disabled**
  in favour of the custom overlay above. Colours validated with the dataviz palette
  script (CVD ΔE 57.8, contrast ≥ 3:1); identity carried by position + brackets,
  not colour alone.
- **Verification:** `SpendingChart.svelte.spec.ts` (8 tests) renders it in Chromium
  and asserts: a bar per Grouping lays out, the once-only Importance brackets, the
  per-bar value labels, expand-in-place (siblings stay), several open at once,
  collapse back, **the bar itself (not just the bracket) expands**, and **the hover
  tooltip shows name + month totals + grand total**. `spendingChart.spec.ts`
  (6 tests) covers the pure accordion model; `spendingReport.spec.ts` (21) the
  aggregation.

**Chart known limitation:**

- **Prior-period comparison** (a **faded prior-year bar side by side** with each
  current-year bar) is now **built** behind the `Compare` toggle — see
  [Year-over-year comparison](#year-over-year-comparison--table-columns--bar-marker-built-).
  Month-by-month detail still lives in the Table view and the hover tooltip; a
  dedicated cumulative-pace trend chart remains the natural home for it (deferred).

## Drill from a table cell into the Expenses view — built ✅

The table's numbers are a jumping-off point (v0.55): clicking a non-blank cell
navigates to the **Expenses** view, filtered to exactly the Expenses that
produced that number.

- **Category detail cell** (category × month) → that **category** in that
  **month**. **Category "Year to Date" cell** → that category across the year.
- **Subtotal cells** roll the filter up to match what they sum:
  - **Grouping subtotal** → every category id in that Grouping (that month/YTD).
  - **Importance subtotal** → every category id across the Importance's groups.
  - **Grand Total** → the date range alone (no category filter) so it ties out to
    all Expenses, **including Uncategorized**.
  - **Uncategorized** cells → the `filter=uncategorized` Expenses filter. A
    named-but-ungrouped category row instead drills to its own category id
    (precise); only the section subtotal and the "(No category)" row use the
    coarse `filter=uncategorized` (which by design covers only null-category
    Expenses, so a subtotal with ungrouped-category rows is a slight over-scope).
- **What shipped.**
  - **Pure** `buildSpendingDrilldownParams(scope, column, year, categories, groups)`
    → `URLSearchParams` in `src/lib/utils/spendingDrilldown.ts`; the scope
    (category / group / importance / uncategorized / grandTotal) and column
    (a month or YTD) come from the clicked row. 8 unit tests in
    `spendingDrilldown.spec.ts`.
  - **Report identity.** `buildSpendingReport` rows/sections now carry the ids the
    drill-down needs: `ReportRow.categoryId`, `GroupSection.id`,
    `ImportanceSection.id` (additive; 6 new tests, 27 total in
    `spendingReport.spec.ts`).
  - **Page.** `/spending` table cells render as `<a href>` links to `/expenses?…`;
    **blank cells (count 0) are not links**.
- **Real Expenses-page contract** (corrects the earlier guess): the params are
  **`dateFrom`/`dateTo`** (inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD`, via `readDateFilter`), category
  is **`category=id,id`**, and uncategorized is **`filter=uncategorized`** — which
  takes precedence over `category`, so the two are never set together.
- **Not yet:** the same affordance on chart bars (deferred). Verified live by the
  maintainer (no auth/seed harness for an end-to-end render pass), like v1.

## Editable hierarchy — assign & re-parent — built ✅

An **Edit hierarchy** page at **`/spending/hierarchy`** (linked from a button on
`/spending`) lets the maintainer restructure the hierarchy without SQL (v0.65).
This directly closes the "Known open item" above: custom/renamed categories that
the name-based seed left in Uncategorized can now be pulled into a Grouping in
the UI.

- **Two mutations shipped** (the highest-value slice):
  - **Assign a Category to a Grouping** (or back to Uncategorized) — a per-category
    `<select>` grouped by Importance via `<optgroup>`.
    `CategoryService.assignCategoryToGroup(categoryId, groupId | null)`.
  - **Move a Grouping to another Area of Importance** — a per-group `<select>`.
    Because Importance attaches to the Grouping, this re-buckets all the group's
    categories at once. `CategoryService.moveGroupToImportance(groupId, importanceAreaId)`.
- **Unassigned bucket up top.** Categories with no `group_id` render in an amber
  "Unassigned categories (N)" section — the editor's whole reason to exist — each
  with the same group picker. Below it, the full Importance → Grouping → Category
  tree with **zero-activity rows NOT suppressed** (unlike the report; every group
  and category must be assignable).
- **Architecture mirrors the report.** Pure `buildHierarchyTree(importanceAreas,
groups, categories) → { importances, unassigned }` in
  `src/lib/utils/hierarchyTree.ts` shapes the three flat tables into the nested
  tree (Importance by `sort_order`, Groupings/Categories alphabetical; orphan
  groups whose Importance FK doesn't resolve fold into a trailing synthetic node
  so nothing is silently dropped). Presentation is a pure
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte` (props in, `onAssignCategory`/`onMoveGroup` out); the
  page owns loading + the CategoryService calls and reloads after each mutation.
  The page self-seeds the hierarchy if empty, like `/spending`.
- **Verification.** `hierarchyTree.spec.ts` (8, pure tree) +
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec.ts` (5, renders the bucket/sections and asserts the
  selects emit the right ids incl. assign-to-null). `check`/eslint/Prettier clean;
  full suite green; production build succeeds. Live end-to-end pass by the
  maintainer (no auth/seed harness), like the earlier slices.

- **Assign-on-create (v0.66).** The inline "Create new category…" form in
  `CategoryDropdown` (expenses page) now offers an optional **Group** selector, so
  a category can be filed into a Grouping at birth instead of landing in
  Uncategorized. `CategoryService.createCategory` gained an optional 4th `groupId`
  arg; the expenses page loads the family's Groupings and passes them in. The
  selector is hidden when no Groupings are supplied, so the receipt/reconciliation
  uses of `CategoryDropdown` (which don't pass `groups`) are unchanged. Tests: 3
  new in `CategoryDropdown.svelte.spec.ts`, 2 in `CategoryService.spec.ts`.

- **Add & rename Groupings (v0.67).** The editor now creates new Groupings and
  renames existing ones, so the tier is no longer SQL-only. An **"Add a Grouping"**
  form (name + Area of Importance) sits below the tree
  (`CategoryService.createGroup(familyId, name, importanceAreaId)`); the new empty
  group appears in its area, ready to have categories assigned into it. Each
  Grouping header has an inline **Rename** (`CategoryService.renameGroup(groupId,
name)`) — safe because the report and editor key off the group id, not its name.
  Both service methods validate the name and map the unique-per-family `23505`
  violation to a friendly message. Tests: 4 new in `CategoryService.spec.ts`
  (create + rename, validation, duplicate-name), 3 in
  `HierarchyEditor.svelte.spec.ts` (add emits name+area, add stays disabled until
  both set, rename emits the edited name).

**Out of scope — the Importance tier is fixed, permanently.** The 3 seeded areas
(Essential / Priorities / Other) will **not** change: there is no add/rename/
reorder UI and none is planned — this is a settled product decision, not a
deferral. Treat Importance-area CRUD as a non-goal.

**Still deferred (Groupings):** Groupings have **no delete** — an empty Grouping
is inert since the report suppresses zero-activity rows, so deleting it (and the
delete-confirmation it would need) buys nothing. Grouping `sort_order` reorder is
also unbuilt (Groupings render alphabetically). Revisit only if a real need
appears.

## Historical-year expense upload — built ✅

A **Import Expenses** page at **`/expenses/import`** (buttons on both `/expenses`
and `/spending`) imports historical Expenses from a CSV / XLS / XLSX file. This
is the keystone of the year-over-year thread: it's the only way to
get prior years' Expenses into the app so the deferred prior-period overlay /
YoY slices have data to compare against.

- **File format.** Columns `Timestamp, Merchant, Amount, Category` (a `Tag`
  column is parsed-and-dropped — there is no tag concept in the schema). `Amount`
  keeps its sign: **positive = expense, negative = refund**, the same convention
  as `receipts.total_amount`, so refunds net against spend exactly as real
  receipts do (no inversion, no `abs()`). `Category` is a plain name; blank →
  Uncategorized.
- **Each row becomes an imageless receipt + a category link.** No schema change
  was needed: `receipts.receipt_image_path` is nullable and `createManual`
  already creates receipts with no image and `suspicious_date` forced `false`
  (these are intentional old entries). A row is one `receipts` insert plus, when
  it has a category, one `expense_categories` upsert (`source: 'manual'`).
  Category names resolve against the family's categories case-insensitively;
  genuinely new names are **created** and land in Uncategorized until filed in
  the hierarchy editor.
- **Two-step preview → confirm.** Unlike the transaction importer (which commits
  straight to the DB), this shows a preview first: how many expenses will import,
  how many duplicates will be skipped, which new categories will be created (with
  a warning + link to the hierarchy editor), and any unreadable rows. Nothing is
  written until the maintainer confirms.
- **Re-import is safe (count-based dedup).** `computeExpenseImportPlan` keys on
  `date | merchant | amount | category` and inserts only `max(0, fileCount −
dbCount)` per key, scoping the existing-rows query to the file's date range —
  re-running the same file is a no-op.
- **Architecture mirrors the report** (pure core + imperative shell). Pure:
  `parseExpenseImportCsv` (`src/lib/utils/expenseImportCsv.ts`),
  `computeExpenseImportPlan` + `buildExpenseCategoryLinks`
  (`src/lib/utils/expenseImportPlan.ts`). Shell: `ExpenseImportService`
  (`buildPreview`/`previewFromText` → `commit`). Reuse: the bank-parser CSV
  primitives (tokenizer, date, amount) were **extracted** from `BaseCSVParser`
  into `src/lib/utils/csvPrimitives.ts` (base now delegates; the 7 bank-parser
  suites are the oracle) so the tokenizer isn't duplicated; `ExcelToCSVConverter`
  handles XLS/XLSX.
- **Verification.** 14 tests `expenseImportCsv.spec.ts`, 12
  `expenseImportPlan.spec.ts`, 7 `ExpenseImportService.spec.ts` (a purpose-built
  Supabase fake dispatching by table/op). `check`/eslint/Prettier clean; full
  suite green; the 229 bank-parser tests still pass after the primitive
  extraction. Live end-to-end pass by the maintainer (no auth/seed harness), like
  the earlier slices.

## Year-over-year comparison — table columns & bar marker built ✅

Now that historical years can be uploaded, the report can show **how spending
changed vs. prior years**. This section catalogues the visualization options,
then records what shipped first.

### The parity rule (load-bearing — governs every option)

Every comparison shares one primitive: a **period cutoff** derived from the
selected year's own data, applied identically to each comparison year.

- **Cutoff = the selected year's last visible month** — the same `maxMonth` the
  report already computes for the rightmost ("Year to Date") column. Reused, not
  re-derived.
- Each comparison year is summed **January → cutoff month only**. A partial 2026
  (Jan–Jul) is compared against **Jan–Jul** of the prior year, never its full
  Jan–Dec — so a half-finished current year can't lose by construction.
- **Whole months only** (the shipped choice). Today being 2026-07-10, July is
  partial in 2026 but was complete in 2025; the month-boundary rule compares
  Jan–Jul wholesale rather than clipping both to Jul 10. Simpler, matches the
  monthly grid, and is what the maintainer asked to start with. A day-boundary
  "pace" comparison is possible later (see the cumulative line below) but is not
  built.

### The options (cheapest → richest)

1. **YoY table column** — after "Year to Date", a single **Change** column
   (Δ amount + % vs the same Jan→cutoff period last year). Same roll-up levels as
   today (category / group / importance / grand total). Pure extension of the
   aggregate; no new chart infra. **Built (below)** — a separate Prior-YTD column
   was prototyped but dropped as redundant (the change alone carries the signal;
   the prior total remains one hover away in the chart tooltip).
2. **Prior-period marker on the magnitude bars** — a horizontal tick / ghost line
   at each bar's prior-YTD value; the gap between bar top and tick _is_ the
   change, read in place with the accordion still working. **Built (below).**
3. **Cumulative "pace" line chart** — x = month (Jan → cutoff), y = running
   cumulative spend, **one line per year** overlaid, every line stopping at the
   same cutoff x so the parity rule is visually self-evident. The natural home
   for the month/time story deliberately dropped off the bars. **Deferred.**
4. **Diverging change bars** — one bar per Grouping = Δ vs prior YTD, increases
   one way / decreases the other, sorted by magnitude; best for _what_ changed.
   **Deferred.** (Colour caution: the app already binds red = expense /
   green = refund, so a diverging chart must not reuse red/green for
   direction — use a neutral diverging pair or encode direction by side + sign.)
5. **Waterfall / bridge** — prior-YTD total → one ±step per Grouping →
   current-YTD total; decomposes the entire YoY change. Richest, least reuse.
   **Built as a horizontal bridge, then ABANDONED as not intuitive** — see
   [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md). Do not
   rebuild it; if "what changed, ranked" is wanted, prefer option 4.

Deliberately skipped: month×grouping heatmaps and indexed-to-100 growth curves —
legible only to spreadsheet-native users, and this report exists to _replace_ the
family's manual pivot, not re-create its density.

### What shipped (options 1 + 2; option 5 abandoned)

- **Toggle.** A **`Compare {priorYear}`** button in the header (next to
  Table | Chart) turns the comparison on/off for **both** views. When the prior
  year has **no data**, the toggle still renders but is **disabled** with an
  explanatory `title` ("No {priorYear} data to compare"). Effective state is
  `comparing = compare && hasPrior`, so stepping the year selector onto a year
  whose predecessor has no data silently disables it and re-enables on return.
  Comparison is **local page state** (like the Table | Chart toggle), not URL —
  it doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.
- **Pure core.** `withPriorPeriod(report, priorReport)` in
  `src/lib/utils/spendingComparison.ts` attaches `priorYtd` (optional field added
  to `ReportRow`) to every row/subtotal/grand-total by summing the prior report's
  cells over the first `report.months.length` months (the parity window), matched
  by **id** (categoryId / groupId / importanceId) with `(No category)` matched by
  name. `spendingChange(current, prior) → { delta, pct, direction }` computes the
  Change cell (pct is `null` when prior is 0 → rendered "new"); `hasPriorData`
  gates the toggle. Both are unit-tested (`spendingComparison.spec.ts`).
- **Table.** A single **Change** column folds into the existing `valueCells`
  snippet so every row type gets it; it shows a signed amount + % coloured by
  direction (increase / decrease / flat) — no user-facing legend copy. The
  Importance/Uncategorized band `colspan`s widen by 1 when comparing. (The
  Prior-YTD column was dropped as redundant — see option 1.)
- **Chart.** `buildSpendingChart` carries `priorTotal` onto each `ChartBar`
  (from the group/category `priorYtd`); `SpendingChart` (new `compare` prop) shows
  a **faded prior-year bar side by side** with each current-year bar, and adds the
  prior total + change to the hover tooltip. (The bars are drawn as scale-derived
  overlays and LayerChart's own bars hidden via `props.bars.opacity`, so current
  and prior can sit side by side; the y-domain is sized to the taller of the two
  years. Superseded the first cut — a dashed prior-period line — which read as an
  ambiguous threshold.) Data loading fetches the prior year's expenses alongside
  the current year's (volume is negligible per the aggregate's own design note),
  so switching the toggle repaints instantly with no refetch.
- **Bridge (option 5) — built, then ABANDONED.** ⚠️ This view was built and pulled
  because **users didn't understand it intuitively** — see
  [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) and the
  reminder screenshot [`docs/BridgeChartTooWide.png`](../BridgeChartTooWide.png).
  The description below is kept as a record of what was tried; the code
  (`SpendingBridge.svelte`, `spendingWaterfall.ts`, their specs, and the `Bridge`
  toggle) has been **removed**. **Do not rebuild it.** A **horizontal waterfall**
  with the **areas on the Y-axis** and the running cumulative amount on the
  X-axis: the top anchor is the prior-year same-period grand total, one floating
  step per area (up = spent more / down = spent less, same red/green as the Change
  column), the bottom anchor is the current-year grand total — the steps always
  reconcile.
  - **Pure core** `buildWaterfallBridge(current, prior, expandedGroups)` in
    `src/lib/utils/spendingWaterfall.ts`. Unlike the magnitude chart it reads
    **both** reports and walks the **union** of groups/categories across the two
    years, so a **disappeared** area (spent last year, nothing this year — no
    current row) still appears as its own downward step. Prior totals use the same
    whole-month parity window. Reconciliation holds at every level: Σ step deltas =
    current − prior grand total. 10 unit tests (`spendingWaterfall.spec.ts`).
  - **Accordion preserved.** Expanding a Grouping emits a **header row** (which
    keeps the − collapse toggle and shows the group's net change at 40 % opacity)
    followed by its Category steps in place; because the category deltas sum to the
    group delta, the running total on either side is unchanged. Many open at once
    (`SvelteSet`), like the magnitude chart.
  - **Rendering** is a self-contained `SpendingBridge.svelte` — percentage-scaled
    off the model's running-total domain (no width measurement, resizes for free),
    Importance colour on the row's left border + a legend, hover tooltip with
    current / prior / change. Only reachable when the prior year has data (the
    `Bridge` toggle is disabled otherwise). 3 render tests.

**Known limitations (documented, not bugs).**

- **Disappeared spend is invisible in the table & chart.** The Change column and
  the side-by-side prior bar both hang off the _current_ report's rows, so a
  Grouping/Category that had spend last year but none this year has no row/bar to
  annotate. The Grand-Total row still reflects it. (The abandoned Bridge view
  surfaced it as a downward step — the one thing only that view did; if it's
  wanted again, build **diverging change bars**, not a waterfall. See
  [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md).)
- **Whole-month only** (see the parity rule) — the current partial month is
  compared against the prior year's _full_ same month.

## Deferred (later slices)

- ~~Prior-period overlay line + year-over-year comparison~~ — **built ✅** (a table
  Change column + a prior-period bar marker), see
  [Year-over-year comparison](#year-over-year-comparison--table-columns--bar-marker-built-).
  A third **Bridge / waterfall** view was built and **abandoned as not intuitive**
  ([ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md)). Richer YoY
  views remain deferred: **cumulative pace line**, **diverging change bars**.
- ~~Historical-year expense upload~~ — **built ✅**, see section above.
- Arbitrary period / quarter selection (beyond a single calendar year).
- The multi-chart-type menu and any second chart type (trend, magnitude).
- Hierarchy tier CRUD — mostly built (assign + re-parent, and now **add/rename
  Groupings**, v0.67). **Importance-area CRUD is a permanent non-goal** — the 3
  seeded areas are fixed and will not change. Not built (but possible later):
  **Grouping delete** (empty groups are inert) and **Grouping reorder**
  (`sort_order`). See the Editable-hierarchy section above.
- Export (CSV / PDF).
- Promoting the report to the home page.

## Known limitations (document when building)

- **Refunds.** Refunds are represented as **negative `total_amount`** on a
  receipt (confirmed via `formatCurrency.spec.ts` and the export services). The
  report **keeps the sign**, so refunds net against spend — which is the correct
  behaviour for a spending total. (Note the CSV/PDF _exporters_ deliberately
  `abs()` refunds; the report does not.) One visible consequence: a Category or
  Grouping whose refunds exceed its spend in the window shows a **negative**
  total — informative, not a bug. No special handling needed in v1; documented
  here so the divergence from the exporters is intentional and searchable.
- **"Year to Date" label** reads oddly for a _completed past_ year (it is the
  full-year total). This was written off as "not a v1 problem since v1 is
  current-year only" — **that premise expired** when historical-year import
  shipped, so a family that has imported 2024 now sees "Year to Date" over a
  full-year column. The heading is still hardcoded
  (`src/routes/spending/+page.svelte:384`); relabel it per-context.

content.text:
I've read the design and the code. Before questions, here's what I confirmed:

- Period today = `?year=YYYY`, parsed in `+page.ts` `load` (`parseYearParam`); columns are Jan → **last month with data**; right-most column hardcoded "Year to Date".
- `SpendingReport.months` is `number[]` (bare 1–12) and `spendingDrilldown` derives date bounds from `(year, column i+1)` — both assume a single calendar year.
- `SpendingChart` only consumes `monthLabels: string[]`, so it's insulated *if* labels stay unique (a cross-year period forces year-qualified labels — two "Jul"s would collide).
- `withPriorPeriod` matches cells positionally by index, so a period shifted back 12 months aligns index-for-index — that generalises cleanly.
- **The Spending nav tab links to bare `/spending`** (`+layout.svelte:99`) — it does *not* use `filterQuery`. So your requirement 3 is already broken today for `year` via the tab route, and won't be fixed by URL params alone.

Starting the grill.

content.text:
Fair challenge — and there's a stronger argument for URL-only than I gave. The design doc records **three failed client-side attempts** at owning the year (onMount read, `$derived` off `$page`, `$derived` off `$app/state`), all fixed by making `load` the single source of truth. localStorage reintroduces exactly that class of thing: a second source of truth plus a `goto` on mount. That's a real reason to stay URL-only.

The honest cost of URL-only: the layout can only forward what's in the *current* URL, so the period has to be threaded through the drill-down URL to come back. That covers the Spending → Expenses → tab journey you named, but not Receipts → Spending or a bare `/spending` bookmark, which reset to the default.

questions.question: Given that — stay URL-only?

options.label: URL-only, thread through drill-down (Recommended)
options.description: Drill-down links carry periodFrom/periodTo alongside dateFrom/dateTo (distinct names so the two don't read as the same filter; Expenses ignores them), and the layout's Spending tab forwards them the same way filterQuery already forwards date filters. Keeps `load` the only source of truth. Accepts that entering /spending from anywhere else resets to the default period.

options.label: URL-only, no threading
options.description: Period lives in ?from/?to and nothing else. Back, refresh and shared links keep it; clicking the Spending tab from Expenses resets to the default period. Zero new machinery — requirement 3 is met for Back only.

options.label: URL-first + localStorage fallback
options.description: As originally proposed: URL wins when present, storage fills the gap when absent. Covers every entry path, at the cost of a second source of truth and a replaceState on mount — the pattern that failed three times for the year.

content.text:
All decisions are in. Here's the shared understanding — confirm and I'll write it into the design doc (doc only; no code).

**Period semantics**
- Whole months, both endpoints inclusive, **max 12 months**. "July → July" = Jul 2025 → Jun 2026.
- URL: `?from=2025-07&to=2026-06`. Legacy `?year=2025` still parses (→ `2025-01`/`2025-12`).
- Default when absent: **current calendar year**, unchanged.
- Bad params: unparseable / inverted → default; over-long → keep start, clamp to 12. Resolved period is `replaceState`'d back so URL and picker agree.

**Columns**
- Every month in the period gets a column; months entirely in the future are dropped. Empty *interior* months render blank.
- Labels year-qualified **only** when the period spans two calendar years (`Jul 25 … Jun 26`); a single-year period looks exactly as today.
- Right-most column becomes **"Total"** with the period in its `title` — this retires the "Year to Date reads wrong" known limitation.

**Picker**
- Four `<select>`s: `From [Jul][2025] To [Jun][2026]`. Moving From drags To along to preserve the span; To clamped to `[From, From+11]`. Not a flowbite `Datepicker` case (month granularity), and no raw `<input type="date">`.
- ← → arrows stay, shifting the window by its own length — identical to today's year arrows for a 12-month period.

**Compare**
- One dropdown: `Off / vs {same period last year} / vs {immediately preceding period}`, dates spelled out. The two modes coincide at 12 months, so only one is offered then. A mode whose window has no data is disabled with the existing explanatory `title`. Stays local page state, per the existing rationale.

**Round-trip (requirement 3)**
- URL-only — no localStorage. `load` stays the single source of truth (the doc already records three failed client-side attempts).
- Drill-down links carry `periodFrom`/`periodTo` alongside `dateFrom`/`dateTo`; the layout's Spending tab forwards them the way `filterQuery` forwards date filters. Deliberately distinct names so they don't read as the same filter.
- **Accepted gap:** entering `/spending` from anywhere else (Receipts tab, bare bookmark) resets to the default period.

**Blast radius** (for the doc's benefit)
- `spendingYear.ts` → period parser; `SpendingReport.months: number[]` → `{year, month}[]` and `year` → `period`; `DrilldownColumn`'s month becomes absolute; `buildSpendingReport` takes a period. `withPriorPeriod` is untouched in mechanism — it matches positionally, so a shifted prior report aligns index-for-index.
- Data loading simplifies: **one** fetch over `period start − 12 months → period end`, three builds off it (current, prior-year, prior-period), replacing today's two fetches.
- `+layout.svelte` gains the forwarder. Touched specs: `spendingYear`, `spendingReport` (27), `spendingComparison`, `spendingDrilldown` (8), `spendingChart`, `SpendingChart.svelte`.
- Quarters explicitly dropped from Deferred.

**One assumption I made rather than asked:** the year `<select>`s offer current year + 1 down to current year − 10. Say the word if you'd rather derive the range from the family's oldest expense.

Noted — the picker's year range comes from the data, not a fixed window.

That needs a fact I checked: **there's no existing "earliest expense" query.** `ExpenseService` has `getExpenses` (which only ever fetches the selected period) and nothing that reports the family's data bounds. So this adds one cheap query — a single-row `transaction_date` min/max on `receipts`, family-scoped by RLS, run in parallel with the existing loads. It can't be derived from the loaded expenses, since those are exactly the period you're already looking at.

Two details I'll write down unless you object:
- Range is **min(earliest expense year, current year) → max(latest expense year, current year)** — symmetric, so a future-dated receipt (which the app already flags) doesn't fall outside the picker, and a family with no expenses still gets the current year.
- If the URL names a year outside that range, the period still renders — the range bounds the *picker*, not what's addressable. Otherwise a stale link would silently snap to the default.

input.new_string:
## Period selection — designed, not built

The report is locked to one calendar year (`?year=`). This slice replaces that
with a **selectable period of whole months, up to twelve** — Jul 2025 → Jun 2026.
**Quarters are dropped as a non-goal**, not deferred: a quarter is a 3-month
period the picker already expresses.

### The period

- **Whole months, both endpoints inclusive, 12 maximum.** "July → July" means
  Jul 2025 → Jun 2026, _not_ a 13th column — a 13-month window would
  double-count July and make the year-over-year comparison overlap its own first
  month.
- **URL: `?from=2025-07&to=2026-06`**, read in the `+page.ts` `load` exactly as
  `?year=` is today. `load` stays the **single source of truth**; the three
  failed client-side attempts recorded under
  [Implementation status](#implementation-status-) are why, and nothing here
  reintroduces a second one (no storage, no read-once-in-`onMount`).
- **Legacy `?year=2025` still parses** (→ `from=2025-01&to=2025-12`), so live and
  bookmarked URLs keep working.
- **Default** when the URL carries neither: the **current calendar year** —
  unchanged landing view, unchanged narrow month labels.
- **Bad input:** unparseable, half-missing, or `from` after `to` falls back to the
  default; a valid but over-long range **keeps its start and clamps to 12
  months** (a hand-edited 18-month link should show roughly what was asked for,
  not snap to "this year"). Whatever it resolves to is `replaceState`d back into
  the URL so the address bar and the picker agree.

### Columns

- **Every month of the period gets a column, except months entirely in the
  future**, which are dropped. Empty interior months still render blank. This
  replaces "January → last month that has any expense": a period the user
  explicitly chose must not silently render shorter than they asked, but neither
  should it show columns for months that haven't happened.
  - Visible consequence: a completed past year with no December spend now shows
    an **empty Dec column** where today it shows none.
- **Month labels are year-qualified only when the period spans two calendar
  years** (`Jul 25 … Jun 26`); a single-year period keeps today's narrow
  `Jan Feb Mar…`. This is not cosmetic — `buildSpendingChart` keys bars by label,
  so two unqualified "Jul"s would collide on the band scale.
- The hardcoded **"Year to Date"** heading becomes **"Total"**, with the period in
  its `title`. This **retires** the known limitation below rather than deferring
  it a third time.

### Picker

Four `<select>`s — `From [Jul] [2025]  To [Jun] [2026]`. Moving `From` drags `To`
along to preserve the current span; `To` is clamped to `[From, From+11]`. Month
granularity is not a `<Datepicker>` case and raw `<input type="date">` is banned,
so plain selects are correct here. The **← → arrows stay**, now shifting the
window by its own length — identical to today's year arrows for a 12-month
period.

**The year options come from the family's data**, not a fixed window:
`min(earliest expense year, current year) → max(latest expense year, current
year)`. This needs a **new one-row min/max `transaction_date` query** on
`ExpenseService`; it cannot be derived from the loaded expenses, which are by
definition just the period already on screen. Symmetric bounds keep a
future-dated receipt (already flagged by `suspicious_date`) inside the picker,
and a family with no expenses still gets the current year. The range bounds the
**picker only** — a URL naming a year outside it still renders, so a stale link
never snaps silently to the default.

### Comparison gains a second mode

The `Compare {priorYear}` button becomes one dropdown — **Off / vs {same period
last year} / vs {immediately preceding period}** — with the actual dates spelled
out in each option.

- **Same period last year** shifts the window back exactly 12 months whatever its
  length. This is the [parity rule](#the-parity-rule-load-bearing--governs-every-option)
  generalized, and it is what keeps the report a year-over-year one.
- **Previous period** shifts back by the period's own length (Oct–Dec vs Jul–Sep).
  Useful on a short period, seasonally meaningless on any period, hence offered
  _alongside_ rather than instead.
- **The two coincide at 12 months**, so a 12-month period offers only one. A mode
  whose window has no data is disabled with the existing explanatory `title`, and
  comparison stays **local page state** for the reason already recorded — it
  doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.

### Surviving the round trip — URL only, deliberately

- Back and refresh already work through `load`; nothing changes there.
- The **Spending nav tab links to a bare `/spending`** (`+layout.svelte`) and so
  drops the period — already true of `?year=` today. Fix: drill-down links carry
  **`periodFrom` / `periodTo`** alongside `dateFrom` / `dateTo`, and the layout's
  Spending link forwards them the way `filterQuery` already forwards date
  filters. The names are deliberately distinct: the Expenses page ignores them,
  and on the same URL they must not read as the same filter.
- **Accepted gap:** entering `/spending` from any other path — the Receipts tab, a
  bare bookmark — resets to the default period. Closing it would need a
  client-side store, which is exactly the pattern that failed three times for the
  year.

### What it touches

- `spendingYear.ts` becomes a period parser (`parseYearParam` → a `Period` parse
  with the legacy `year` branch).
- `SpendingReport.year` → a `period`; `months: number[]` → `{ year, month }[]`;
