## Period selection — designed, not built

The report is locked to one calendar year (`?year=`). This slice replaces that
with a **selectable period of whole months, up to twelve** — Jul 2025 → Jun 2026.
**Quarters are dropped as a non-goal**, not deferred: a quarter is a 3-month
period the picker already expresses.

### The period

- **Whole months, both endpoints inclusive, 12 maximum.** "July → July" means
  Jul 2025 → Jun 2026, _not_ a 13th column — a 13-month window would
  double-count July and make the year-over-year comparison overlap its own first
  month.
- **URL: `?from=2025-07&to=2026-06`**, read in the `+page.ts` `load` exactly as
  `?year=` is today. `load` stays the **single source of truth**; the three
  failed client-side attempts recorded under
  [Implementation status](#implementation-status-) are why, and nothing here
  reintroduces a second one (no storage, no read-once-in-`onMount`).
- **Legacy `?year=2025` still parses** (→ `from=2025-01&to=2025-12`), so live and
  bookmarked URLs keep working.
- **Default** when the URL carries neither: the **current calendar year** —
  unchanged landing view, unchanged narrow month labels.
- **Bad input:** unparseable, half-missing, or `from` after `to` falls back to the
  default; a valid but over-long range **keeps its start and clamps to 12
  months** (a hand-edited 18-month link should show roughly what was asked for,
  not snap to "this year"). Whatever it resolves to is `replaceState`d back into
  the URL so the address bar and the picker agree.

### Columns

- **Every month of the period gets a column, except months entirely in the
  future**, which are dropped. Empty interior months still render blank. This
  replaces "January → last month that has any expense": a period the user
  explicitly chose must not silently render shorter than they asked, but neither
  should it show columns for months that haven't happened.
  - Visible consequence: a completed past year with no December spend now shows
    an **empty Dec column** where today it shows none.
- **Month labels are year-qualified only when the period spans two calendar
  years** (`Jul 25 … Jun 26`); a single-year period keeps today's narrow
  `Jan Feb Mar…`. This is not cosmetic — `buildSpendingChart` keys bars by label,
  so two unqualified "Jul"s would collide on the band scale.
- The hardcoded **"Year to Date"** heading becomes **"Total"**, with the period in
  its `title`. This **retires** the known limitation below rather than deferring
  it a third time.

### Picker

Four `<select>`s — `From [Jul] [2025]  To [Jun] [2026]`. Moving `From` drags `To`
along to preserve the current span; `To` is clamped to `[From, From+11]`. Month
granularity is not a `<Datepicker>` case and raw `<input type="date">` is banned,
so plain selects are correct here. The **← → arrows stay**, now shifting the
window by its own length — identical to today's year arrows for a 12-month
period.

**The year options come from the family's data**, not a fixed window:
`min(earliest expense year, current year) → max(latest expense year, current
year)`. This needs a **new one-row min/max `transaction_date` query** on
`ExpenseService`; it cannot be derived from the loaded expenses, which are by
definition just the period already on screen. Symmetric bounds keep a
future-dated receipt (already flagged by `suspicious_date`) inside the picker,
and a family with no expenses still gets the current year. The range bounds the
**picker only** — a URL naming a year outside it still renders, so a stale link
never snaps silently to the default.

### Comparison gains a second mode

The `Compare {priorYear}` button becomes one dropdown — **Off / vs {same period
last year} / vs {immediately preceding period}** — with the actual dates spelled
out in each option.

- **Same period last year** shifts the window back exactly 12 months whatever its
  length. This is the [parity rule](#the-parity-rule-load-bearing--governs-every-option)
  generalized, and it is what keeps the report a year-over-year one.
- **Previous period** shifts back by the period's own length (Oct–Dec vs Jul–Sep).
  Useful on a short period, seasonally meaningless on any period, hence offered
  _alongside_ rather than instead.
- **The two coincide at 12 months**, so a 12-month period offers only one. A mode
  whose window has no data is disabled with the existing explanatory `title`, and
  comparison stays **local page state** for the reason already recorded — it
  doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.

### Surviving the round trip — URL only, deliberately

- Back and refresh already work through `load`; nothing changes there.
- The **Spending nav tab links to a bare `/spending`** (`+layout.svelte`) and so
  drops the period — already true of `?year=` today. Fix: drill-down links carry
  **`periodFrom` / `periodTo`** alongside `dateFrom` / `dateTo`, and the layout's
  Spending link forwards them the way `filterQuery` already forwards date
  filters. The names are deliberately distinct: the Expenses page ignores them,
  and on the same URL they must not read as the same filter.
- **Accepted gap:** entering `/spending` from any other path — the Receipts tab, a
  bare bookmark — resets to the default period. Closing it would need a
  client-side store, which is exactly the pattern that failed three times for the
  year.

### What it touches

- `spendingYear.ts` becomes a period parser (`parseYearParam` → a `Period` parse
  with the legacy `year` branch).
- `SpendingReport.year` → a `period`; `months: number[]` → `{ year, month }[]`;
  `buildSpendingReport` takes the period instead of a year.
- `spendingDrilldown.ts`: a `DrilldownColumn` month becomes absolute
  (`{ year, month }`) and the `year` parameter drops; the Total column's bounds
  span the whole period.
- **`withPriorPeriod` is untouched in mechanism** — it matches cells
  _positionally_, so a prior report built over a shifted period aligns
  index-for-index. Only its callers change.
- **Loading gets simpler, not harder:** one fetch over `period start − 12 months
→ period end` and three builds off it (current, prior-year, prior-period),
  replacing today's two year-sized fetches.
- Specs to extend: `spendingYear`, `spendingReport`, `spendingComparison`,
  `spendingDrilldown`, `spendingChart`, `SpendingChart.svelte`.

<script lang="ts">
	/**
	 * SpendingChart — an accordion magnitude bar chart of the Spending Report.
	 *
	 * One solid bar per Grouping = its year-to-date total, coloured by Area of
	 * Importance. Each Grouping can be **expanded in place** (via its ± bracket) to
	 * reveal its Category bars while siblings stay visible; any number can be open
	 * at once. Two bracket rows under the axis carry the hierarchy: a per-Grouping
	 * toggle row, then the Area-of-Importance row. Every bar carries a value label
	 * so small bars stay readable next to a dominant one.
	 *
	 * When `compare` is on, each Grouping shows a faded prior-year bar beside the
	 * current-year bar (side by side).
	 *
	 * (Month-by-month detail lives in the Table view and the future trend chart.)
	 *
	 * Built on LayerChart's <BarChart> for scales + axes; the bars themselves are
	 * drawn as overlays (so current/prior sit side by side) and LayerChart's own
	 * bars are hidden. Data shaping is the pure `buildSpendingChart`.
	 * Design: docs/plans/2026-07-09-spending-report-design.md
	 */
	import { BarChart, Text } from 'layerchart';
	import type { ChartState } from 'layerchart';
	import { SvelteSet } from 'svelte/reactivity';
	import { buildSpendingChart, type ChartBar } from '$lib/utils/spendingChart';
	import type { SpendingReport } from '$lib/utils/spendingReport';
	import { spendingChange } from '$lib/utils/spendingComparison';
	import { formatCurrency } from '$lib/utils/formatCurrency';

	// `compare` shows a faded prior-year bar beside each current-year bar (and adds
	// the prior total + change to the tooltip). The prior totals ride along on the
	// report's rows via `withPriorPeriod`; the parent only flips the flag.
	let { report, compare = false }: { report: SpendingReport; compare?: boolean } = $props();

	const priorYear = $derived(report.year - 1);

	// Grouping names currently expanded to their Categories (accordion; many at once).
	const expandedGroups = new SvelteSet<string>();

	const model = $derived(buildSpendingChart(report, expandedGroups));

	function toggleGroup(name: string) {
		if (expandedGroups.has(name)) expandedGroups.delete(name);
		else expandedGroups.add(name);
	}

	// LayerChart data: a stable unique id per bar (names can repeat across groups,
	// which would collide on the band scale), plus the fields the chart reads.
	// LayerChart draws no visible bars (its own bars are hidden — see props.bars);
	// we render them as overlays. `total` here only sizes the y-domain, so when
	// comparing it's the taller of the two years, ensuring a tall prior bar fits.
	const data = $derived(
		model.bars.map((bar, i) => ({
			id: `b${i}`,
			name: bar.name,
			kind: bar.kind,
			importance: bar.importance,
			total: compare ? Math.max(bar.total, bar.priorTotal ?? 0) : bar.total
		}))
	);

content.content:
545	## Period selection — designed, not built
546	
547	The report is locked to one calendar year (`?year=`). This slice replaces that
548	with a **selectable period of whole months, up to twelve** — Jul 2025 → Jun 2026.
549	**Quarters are dropped as a non-goal**, not deferred: a quarter is a 3-month
550	period the picker already expresses.
551	
552	### The period
553	
554	- **Whole months, both endpoints inclusive, 12 maximum.** "July → July" means
555	  Jul 2025 → Jun 2026, _not_ a 13th column — a 13-month window would
556	  double-count July and make the year-over-year comparison overlap its own first
557	  month.
558	- **URL: `?from=2025-07&to=2026-06`**, read in the `+page.ts` `load` exactly as
559	  `?year=` is today. `load` stays the **single source of truth**; the three
560	  failed client-side attempts recorded under
561	  [Implementation status](#implementation-status-) are why, and nothing here
562	  reintroduces a second one (no storage, no read-once-in-`onMount`).
563	- **Legacy `?year=2025` still parses** (→ `from=2025-01&to=2025-12`), so live and
564	  bookmarked URLs keep working.
565	- **Default** when the URL carries neither: the **current calendar year** —
566	  unchanged landing view, unchanged narrow month labels.
567	- **Bad input:** unparseable, half-missing, or `from` after `to` falls back to the
568	  default; a valid but over-long range **keeps its start and clamps to 12
569	  months** (a hand-edited 18-month link should show roughly what was asked for,
570	  not snap to "this year"). Whatever it resolves to is `replaceState`d back into
571	  the URL so the address bar and the picker agree.
572	
573	### Columns
574	
575	- **Every month of the period gets a column, except months entirely in the
576	  future**, which are dropped. Empty interior months still render blank. This
577	  replaces "January → last month that has any expense": a period the user
578	  explicitly chose must not silently render shorter than they asked, but neither
579	  should it show columns for months that haven't happened.
580	  - Visible consequence: a completed past year with no December spend now shows
581	    an **empty Dec column** where today it shows none.
582	- **Month labels are year-qualified only when the period spans two calendar
583	  years** (`Jul 25 … Jun 26`); a single-year period keeps today's narrow
584	  `Jan Feb Mar…`. This is not cosmetic — `buildSpendingChart` keys bars by label,
585	  so two unqualified "Jul"s would collide on the band scale.
586	- The hardcoded **"Year to Date"** heading becomes **"Total"**, with the period in
587	  its `title`. This **retires** the known limitation below rather than deferring
588	  it a third time.
589	
590	### Picker
591	
592	Four `<select>`s — `From [Jul] [2025]  To [Jun] [2026]`. Moving `From` drags `To`
593	along to preserve the current span; `To` is clamped to `[From, From+11]`. Month
594	granularity is not a `<Datepicker>` case and raw `<input type="date">` is banned,
595	so plain selects are correct here. The **← → arrows stay**, now shifting the
596	window by its own length — identical to today's year arrows for a 12-month
597	period.
598	
599	**The year options come from the family's data**, not a fixed window:
600	`min(earliest expense year, current year) → max(latest expense year, current
601	year)`. This needs a **new one-row min/max `transaction_date` query** on
602	`ExpenseService`; it cannot be derived from the loaded expenses, which are by
603	definition just the period already on screen. Symmetric bounds keep a
604	future-dated receipt (already flagged by `suspicious_date`) inside the picker,
605	and a family with no expenses still gets the current year. The range bounds the
606	**picker only** — a URL naming a year outside it still renders, so a stale link
607	never snaps silently to the default.
608	
609	### Comparison gains a second mode
610	
611	The `Compare {priorYear}` button becomes one dropdown — **Off / vs {same period
612	last year} / vs {immediately preceding period}** — with the actual dates spelled
613	out in each option.
614	
615	- **Same period last year** shifts the window back exactly 12 months whatever its
616	  length. This is the [parity rule](#the-parity-rule-load-bearing--governs-every-option)
617	  generalized, and it is what keeps the report a year-over-year one.
618	- **Previous period** shifts back by the period's own length (Oct–Dec vs Jul–Sep).
619	  Useful on a short period, seasonally meaningless on any period, hence offered
620	  _alongside_ rather than instead.
621	- **The two coincide at 12 months**, so a 12-month period offers only one. A mode
622	  whose window has no data is disabled with the existing explanatory `title`, and
623	  comparison stays **local page state** for the reason already recorded — it
624	  doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.
625	
626	### Surviving the round trip — URL only, deliberately
627	
628	- Back and refresh already work through `load`; nothing changes there.
629	- The **Spending nav tab links to a bare `/spending`** (`+layout.svelte`) and so
630	  drops the period — already true of `?year=` today. Fix: drill-down links carry
631	  **`periodFrom` / `periodTo`** alongside `dateFrom` / `dateTo`, and the layout's
632	  Spending link forwards them the way `filterQuery` already forwards date
633	  filters. The names are deliberately distinct: the Expenses page ignores them,
634	  and on the same URL they must not read as the same filter.
635	- **Accepted gap:** entering `/spending` from any other path — the Receipts tab, a
636	  bare bookmark — resets to the default period. Closing it would need a
637	  client-side store, which is exactly the pattern that failed three times for the
638	  year.
639	
640	### What it touches
641	
642	- `spendingYear.ts` becomes a period parser (`parseYearParam` → a `Period` parse
643	  with the legacy `year` branch).
644	- `SpendingReport.year` → a `period`; `months: number[]` → `{ year, month }[]`;
645	  `buildSpendingReport` takes the period instead of a year.

## Period selection — designed, not built

The report is locked to one calendar year (`?year=`). This slice replaces that
with a **selectable period of whole months, up to twelve** — Jul 2025 → Jun 2026.
**Quarters are dropped as a non-goal**, not deferred: a quarter is a 3-month
period the picker already expresses.

### The period

- **Whole months, both endpoints inclusive, 12 maximum.** "July → July" means
  Jul 2025 → Jun 2026, _not_ a 13th column — a 13-month window would
  double-count July and make the year-over-year comparison overlap its own first
  month.
- **URL: `?from=2025-07&to=2026-06`**, read in the `+page.ts` `load` exactly as
  `?year=` is today. `load` stays the **single source of truth**; the three
  failed client-side attempts recorded under
  [Implementation status](#implementation-status-) are why, and nothing here
  reintroduces a second one (no storage, no read-once-in-`onMount`).
- **Legacy `?year=2025` still parses** (→ `from=2025-01&to=2025-12`), so live and
  bookmarked URLs keep working.
- **Default** when the URL carries neither: the **current calendar year** —
  unchanged landing view, unchanged narrow month labels.
- **Bad input:** unparseable, half-missing, or `from` after `to` falls back to the
  default; a valid but over-long range **keeps its start and clamps to 12
  months** (a hand-edited 18-month link should show roughly what was asked for,
  not snap to "this year"). Whatever it resolves to is `replaceState`d back into
  the URL so the address bar and the picker agree.

### Columns

- **Every month of the period gets a column, except months entirely in the
  future**, which are dropped. Empty interior months still render blank. This
  replaces "January → last month that has any expense": a period the user
  explicitly chose must not silently render shorter than they asked, but neither
  should it show columns for months that haven't happened.
  - Visible consequence: a completed past year with no December spend now shows
    an **empty Dec column** where today it shows none.
- **Month labels are year-qualified only when the period spans two calendar
  years** (`Jul 25 … Jun 26`); a single-year period keeps today's narrow
  `Jan Feb Mar…`. This is not cosmetic — `buildSpendingChart` keys bars by label,
  so two unqualified "Jul"s would collide on the band scale.
- The hardcoded **"Year to Date"** heading becomes **"Total"**, with the period in
  its `title`. This **retires** the known limitation below rather than deferring
  it a third time.

### Picker

Four `<select>`s — `From [Jul] [2025]  To [Jun] [2026]`. Moving `From` drags `To`
along to preserve the current span; `To` is clamped to `[From, From+11]`. Month
granularity is not a `<Datepicker>` case and raw `<input type="date">` is banned,
so plain selects are correct here. The **← → arrows stay**, now shifting the
window by its own length — identical to today's year arrows for a 12-month
period.

**The year options come from the family's data**, not a fixed window:
`min(earliest expense year, current year) → max(latest expense year, current
year)`. This needs a **new one-row min/max `transaction_date` query** on
`ExpenseService`; it cannot be derived from the loaded expenses, which are by
definition just the period already on screen. Symmetric bounds keep a
future-dated receipt (already flagged by `suspicious_date`) inside the picker,
and a family with no expenses still gets the current year. The range bounds the
**picker only** — a URL naming a year outside it still renders, so a stale link
never snaps silently to the default.

### Comparison gains a second mode

The `Compare {priorYear}` button becomes one dropdown — **Off / vs {same period
last year} / vs {immediately preceding period}** — with the actual dates spelled
out in each option.

- **Same period last year** shifts the window back exactly 12 months whatever its
  length. This is the [parity rule](#the-parity-rule-load-bearing--governs-every-option)
  generalized, and it is what keeps the report a year-over-year one.
- **Previous period** shifts back by the period's own length (Oct–Dec vs Jul–Sep).
  Useful on a short period, seasonally meaningless on any period, hence offered
  _alongside_ rather than instead.
- **The two coincide at 12 months**, so a 12-month period offers only one. A mode
  whose window has no data is disabled with the existing explanatory `title`, and
  comparison stays **local page state** for the reason already recorded — it
  doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.

### Surviving the round trip — URL only, deliberately

- Back and refresh already work through `load`; nothing changes there.
- The **Spending nav tab links to a bare `/spending`** (`+layout.svelte`) and so
  drops the period — already true of `?year=` today. Fix: drill-down links carry
  **`periodFrom` / `periodTo`** alongside `dateFrom` / `dateTo`, and the layout's
  Spending link forwards them the way `filterQuery` already forwards date
  filters. The names are deliberately distinct: the Expenses page ignores them,
  and on the same URL they must not read as the same filter.
- **Accepted gap:** entering `/spending` from any other path — the Receipts tab, a
  bare bookmark — resets to the default period. Closing it would need a
  client-side store, which is exactly the pattern that failed three times for the
  year.

### What it touches

- `spendingYear.ts` becomes a period parser (`parseYearParam` → a `Period` parse
  with the legacy `year` branch).
- `SpendingReport.year` → a `period`; `months: number[]` → `{ year, month }[]`;
  `buildSpendingReport` takes the period instead of a year.
- `spendingDrilldown.ts`: a `DrilldownColumn` month becomes absolute
  (`{ year, month }`) and the `year` parameter drops; the Total column's bounds
  span the whole period.
- **`withPriorPeriod` is untouched in mechanism** — it matches cells
  _positionally_, so a prior report built over a shifted period aligns
  index-for-index. Only its callers change.
- **Loading gets simpler, not harder:** one fetch over `period start − 12 months
→ period end` and three builds off it (current, prior-year, prior-period),
  replacing today's two year-sized fetches.
- Specs to extend: `spendingYear`, `spendingReport`, `spendingComparison`,
  `spendingDrilldown`, `spendingChart`, `SpendingChart.svelte`.

## Deferred (later slices)

## Period selection — built ✅

The report used to be locked to one calendar year (`?year=`). It now runs over a
**selectable period of whole months, up to twelve** — Jul 2025 → Jun 2026.
**Quarters are dropped as a non-goal**, not deferred: a quarter is a 3-month
period the picker expresses.

### The period

- **Whole months, both endpoints inclusive, 12 maximum.** "July → July" means
  Jul 2025 → Jun 2026, _not_ a 13th column — a 13-month window would
  double-count July and make the year-over-year comparison overlap its own first
  month.
- **URL: `?from=2025-07&to=2026-06`**, read in the `+page.ts` `load` exactly as
  `?year=` was. `load` stays the **single source of truth**; the three failed
  client-side attempts recorded under
  [Implementation status](#implementation-status-) are why, and nothing here
  reintroduces a second one (no storage, no read-once-in-`onMount`).
- **Legacy `?year=2025` still parses** (→ `from=2025-01&to=2025-12`), so live and
  bookmarked URLs keep working.
- **Default** when the URL carries neither: the **current calendar year** —
  unchanged landing view, unchanged narrow month labels.
- **Bad input:** unparseable, half-missing, or `from` after `to` falls back to the
  default; a valid but over-long range **keeps its start and clamps to 12
  months** (a hand-edited 18-month link should show roughly what was asked for,
  not snap to "this year").
- Anything that isn't already the canonical spelling — no params, the legacy
  `?year=`, a clamped range — **`redirect`s from `load`** to the canonical URL, so
  the address bar and the picker always agree. That redirect is safe only because
  `parsePeriodParams` is **idempotent over `periodParams`**; there is a test
  pinning it, and breaking it would loop.

### Columns

- **Every month of the period gets a column, except trailing months that are both
  in the future _and_ empty.** Empty interior months still render blank. This
  replaces "January → last month that has any expense": a period the reader
  explicitly chose must not silently render shorter than they asked, but neither
  should it paint columns for months that haven't happened.
  - **Why "and empty" rather than a flat cut at today** (a refinement on the
    design as first agreed): this app deliberately allows future-dated receipts
    and merely flags them (`suspicious_date`). A flat cut would drop such a
    receipt out of the visible grid _and_ out of the Grand Total, which is
    supposed to tie out to the family's actual spend. So a future month that has
    data keeps its column.
  - `visibleMonths` also never returns fewer than one month, so a wholly-future
    period renders an empty grid rather than nothing.
  - Visible consequence: a completed past year with no December spend now shows
    an **empty Dec column** where it used to show none.
- **Month labels are year-qualified only when the period spans two calendar
  years** (`Jul 25 … Jun 26`); a single-year period keeps the narrow
  `Jan Feb Mar…`. This is not cosmetic — `buildSpendingChart` keys bars by label,
  so two unqualified "Jul"s would collide on the band scale.
- The hardcoded **"Year to Date"** heading is now **"Total"**, with the period in
  its `title`. That **retires** the known limitation below rather than deferring
  it a third time.

### Picker

`PeriodPicker.svelte` — four `<select>`s, `From [Jul] [2025]  To [Jun] [2026]`.
Month granularity is not a `<Datepicker>` case and raw `<input type="date">` is
banned, so plain selects are correct here. The **← → arrows stay**, now shifting
the window by its own length — identical to the year arrows they replaced for a
12-month period.

Both constraints are **structural rather than corrective**, so nothing snaps back
under the reader: moving `From` drags `To` along to preserve the span, and the
`To` selects only _list_ months inside `[From, From+11]` — which is where the
12-month cap lives in the UI. (Changing the To **year** can still orphan the
month, so that one handler lands on the nearest allowed month.)

**The year options come from the family's data**, not a fixed window:
`min(earliest expense year, current year) → max(latest expense year, current
year)`. That is `ExpenseService.getExpenseDateBounds()`, a new two-row query
(one from each end of the `transaction_date` sort); it cannot be derived from the
loaded expenses, which are by definition just the period already on screen.
Symmetric bounds keep a future-dated receipt inside the picker, and a family with
no expenses still gets the current year. The range bounds the **picker only** — a
URL naming a year outside it still renders, and the picker widens to include it,
so a stale link never snaps silently to the default.

### Comparison gained a second mode

The `Compare {priorYear}` button is now one dropdown — **Off / vs {same period
last year} / vs {immediately preceding period}** — with the actual dates spelled
out in each option.

- **Same period last year** shifts the window back exactly 12 months whatever its
  length. This is the [parity rule](#the-parity-rule-load-bearing--governs-every-option)
  generalized, and it is what keeps the report a year-over-year one.
- **Previous period** shifts back by the period's own length (Oct–Dec vs Jul–Sep).
  Useful on a short period, seasonally meaningless on any period, hence offered
  _alongside_ rather than instead.
- **The two coincide at 12 months**, so a 12-month period offers only one. A mode
  whose window has no data is **not listed at all** (rather than listed-and-
  disabled), so there is no dead state to explain; the whole control disables when
  no mode has data. Comparison stays **local page state** for the reason already
  recorded — it doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.
- A mode can stop being valid when the period changes under it (a 12-month period
  drops `priorPeriod`). The page re-derives the effective mode from the offered
  list rather than trusting the stored one, so it silently falls back to Off and
  comes back on return.
- **`withPriorPeriod` is now non-mutating.** It used to annotate the report in
  place, which was safe when there was one comparison and it was rebuilt per load.
  With a switchable mode the page derives the rendered report from an
  un-annotated `baseReport`, so in-place annotation would strand a stale
  `priorTotal` when the comparison is switched off.

### Surviving the round trip — URL only, deliberately

- Back and refresh work through `load`; nothing changed there.
- The **Spending nav tab used to link to a bare `/spending`** (`+layout.svelte`),
  dropping the period — already true of `?year=`. Drill-down links now carry
  **`periodFrom` / `periodTo`** alongside `dateFrom` / `dateTo`, and the layout's
  Spending link forwards them the way `filterQuery` forwards date filters. The
  names are deliberately distinct: the Expenses page ignores them, and on the same
  URL they must not read as the same filter.
- The **hierarchy editor** is on the same path: `/spending` passes the period to
  `/spending/hierarchy?from=…&to=…` (same names — no `dateFrom` to collide with on
  a spending route) and its "Back to Spending" rebuilds from them. A link href
  derived off `$page` is fine here; it was the *data* that had to come from `load`.
- **Accepted gap:** entering `/spending` from any other path — the Receipts tab, a
  bare bookmark — resets to the default period. Closing it would need a
  client-side store, which is exactly the pattern that failed three times for the
  year.

### What shipped

- **`spendingPeriod.ts`** (replaces `spendingYear.ts`) — `Period` / `YearMonth`,
  `parsePeriodParams` + `periodParams`, `addMonths` / `shiftPeriod` /
  `periodLength` / `periodMonths`, `monthColumnLabels`, `formatPeriod`. No clock:
  "today" is a parameter, as the old fallback year was. 31 tests.
- **`spendingReport.ts`** — `SpendingReport.year` → `period`; `months: number[]` →
  `YearMonth[]`; `ReportRow.ytd` → `total` and `priorYtd` → `priorTotal` (the old
  names lied once the column stopped being year-to-date). `buildSpendingReport`
  takes `(…, period, today)`; `visibleMonths` and `hasReportData` are exported.
  38 tests.
- **`spendingComparison.ts`** — `CompareMode`, `comparisonPeriod`,
  `comparisonModes`, `comparisonLabel`; `withPriorPeriod` made non-mutating. Its
  index/positional matching is otherwise untouched, so a prior report built over a
  shifted period aligns index-for-index. 23 tests.
- **`spendingDrilldown.ts`** — the month column is absolute (`{ year, month }`),
  `ytd` → `total`, and the four context arguments collapse into one
  `DrilldownContext`. The Total column is bounded by the **visible** months (so it
  matches the number clicked), while `periodFrom`/`periodTo` echo the **selected**
  period (so returning restores what was asked for). 14 tests.
- **`PeriodPicker.svelte`** (new, 9 render tests) and the page's compare
  `<select>`; `SpendingChart` takes `periodLabel` / `priorLabel` props instead of
  doing its own `report.year - 1`, keeping period arithmetic out of the chart.
- **`ExpenseService.getExpenseDateBounds()`** (3 tests) for the picker's years.
- **Loading got simpler, not harder:** one fetch over `period start − 12 months →
period end` and three builds off it (current, prior-year, prior-period),
  replacing the two year-sized fetches.
- **Verification:** `npm run verify` clean (check, check:deno, lint, 1456 server
  tests); the browser project passes 150 including the new picker and layout
  specs. Live end-to-end pass by the maintainer, like the earlier slices.

## Period selection — built ✅

The report used to be locked to one calendar year (`?year=`). It now runs over a
**selectable period of whole months, up to twelve** — Jul 2025 → Jun 2026.
**Quarters are dropped as a non-goal**, not deferred: a quarter is a 3-month
period the picker expresses.

### The period

- **Whole months, both endpoints inclusive, 12 maximum.** "July → July" means
  Jul 2025 → Jun 2026, _not_ a 13th column — a 13-month window would
  double-count July and make the year-over-year comparison overlap its own first
  month.
- **URL: `?from=2025-07&to=2026-06`**, read in the `+page.ts` `load` exactly as
  `?year=` was. `load` stays the **single source of truth**; the three failed
  client-side attempts recorded under
  [Implementation status](#implementation-status-) are why, and nothing here
  reintroduces a second one (no storage, no read-once-in-`onMount`).
- **Legacy `?year=2025` still parses** (→ `from=2025-01&to=2025-12`), so live and
  bookmarked URLs keep working.
- **Default** when the URL carries neither: the **current calendar year** —
  unchanged landing view, unchanged narrow month labels.
- **Bad input:** unparseable, half-missing, or `from` after `to` falls back to the
  default; a valid but over-long range **keeps its start and clamps to 12
  months** (a hand-edited 18-month link should show roughly what was asked for,
  not snap to "this year").
- Anything that isn't already the canonical spelling — no params, the legacy
  `?year=`, a clamped range — **`redirect`s from `load`** to the canonical URL, so
  the address bar and the picker always agree. That redirect is safe only because
  `parsePeriodParams` is **idempotent over `periodParams`**; there is a test
  pinning it, and breaking it would loop.

### Columns

- **Every month of the period gets a column, except trailing months that are both
  in the future _and_ empty.** Empty interior months still render blank. This
  replaces "January → last month that has any expense": a period the reader
  explicitly chose must not silently render shorter than they asked, but neither
  should it paint columns for months that haven't happened.
  - **Why "and empty" rather than a flat cut at today** (a refinement on the
    design as first agreed): this app deliberately allows future-dated receipts
    and merely flags them (`suspicious_date`). A flat cut would drop such a
    receipt out of the visible grid _and_ out of the Grand Total, which is
    supposed to tie out to the family's actual spend. So a future month that has
    data keeps its column.
  - `visibleMonths` also never returns fewer than one month, so a wholly-future
    period renders an empty grid rather than nothing.
  - Visible consequence: a completed past year with no December spend now shows
    an **empty Dec column** where it used to show none.
- **Month labels are year-qualified only when the period spans two calendar
  years** (`Jul 25 … Jun 26`); a single-year period keeps the narrow
  `Jan Feb Mar…`. This is not cosmetic — `buildSpendingChart` keys bars by label,
  so two unqualified "Jul"s would collide on the band scale.
- The hardcoded **"Year to Date"** heading is now **"Total"**, with the period in
  its `title`. That **retires** the known limitation below rather than deferring
  it a third time.

### Picker

`PeriodPicker.svelte` — four `<select>`s, `From [Jul] [2025]  To [Jun] [2026]`.
Month granularity is not a `<Datepicker>` case and raw `<input type="date">` is
banned, so plain selects are correct here. The **← → arrows stay**, now shifting
the window by its own length — identical to the year arrows they replaced for a
12-month period.

Both constraints are **structural rather than corrective**, so nothing snaps back
under the reader: moving `From` drags `To` along to preserve the span, and the
`To` selects only _list_ months inside `[From, From+11]` — which is where the
12-month cap lives in the UI. (Changing the To **year** can still orphan the
month, so that one handler lands on the nearest allowed month.)

**The year options come from the family's data**, not a fixed window:
`min(earliest expense year, current year) → max(latest expense year, current
year)`. That is `ExpenseService.getExpenseDateBounds()`, a new two-row query
(one from each end of the `transaction_date` sort); it cannot be derived from the
loaded expenses, which are by definition just the period already on screen.
Symmetric bounds keep a future-dated receipt inside the picker, and a family with
no expenses still gets the current year. The range bounds the **picker only** — a
URL naming a year outside it still renders, and the picker widens to include it,
so a stale link never snaps silently to the default.

### Comparison gained a second mode

The `Compare {priorYear}` button is now one dropdown — **Off / vs {same period
last year} / vs {immediately preceding period}** — with the actual dates spelled
out in each option.

- **Same period last year** shifts the window back exactly 12 months whatever its
  length. This is the [parity rule](#the-parity-rule-load-bearing--governs-every-option)
  generalized, and it is what keeps the report a year-over-year one.
- **Previous period** shifts back by the period's own length (Oct–Dec vs Jul–Sep).
  Useful on a short period, seasonally meaningless on any period, hence offered
  _alongside_ rather than instead.
- **The two coincide at 12 months**, so a 12-month period offers only one. A mode
  whose window has no data is **not listed at all** (rather than listed-and-
  disabled), so there is no dead state to explain; the whole control disables when
  no mode has data. Comparison stays **local page state** for the reason already
  recorded — it doesn't affect drill-down navigation, so it needn't survive Back.
- A mode can stop being valid when the period changes under it (a 12-month period
  drops `priorPeriod`). The page re-derives the effective mode from the offered
  list rather than trusting the stored one, so it silently falls back to Off and
  comes back on return.
- **`withPriorPeriod` is now non-mutating.** It used to annotate the report in
  place, which was safe when there was one comparison and it was rebuilt per load.
  With a switchable mode the page derives the rendered report from an
  un-annotated `baseReport`, so in-place annotation would strand a stale
  `priorTotal` when the comparison is switched off.

### Surviving the round trip — URL only, deliberately

- Back and refresh work through `load`; nothing changed there.
- The **Spending nav tab used to link to a bare `/spending`** (`+layout.svelte`),
  dropping the period — already true of `?year=`. Drill-down links now carry
  **`periodFrom` / `periodTo`** alongside `dateFrom` / `dateTo`, and the layout's
  Spending link forwards them the way `filterQuery` forwards date filters. The
  names are deliberately distinct: the Expenses page ignores them, and on the same
  URL they must not read as the same filter.
- The **hierarchy editor** is on the same path: `/spending` passes the period to
  `/spending/hierarchy?from=…&to=…` (same names — no `dateFrom` to collide with on
  a spending route) and its "Back to Spending" rebuilds from them. A link href
  derived off `$page` is fine here; it was the *data* that had to come from `load`.
- **Accepted gap:** entering `/spending` from any other path — the Receipts tab, a
  bare bookmark — resets to the default period. Closing it would need a
  client-side store, which is exactly the pattern that failed three times for the
  year.

### What shipped

- **`spendingPeriod.ts`** (replaces `spendingYear.ts`) — `Period` / `YearMonth`,
  `parsePeriodParams` + `periodParams`, `addMonths` / `shiftPeriod` /
  `periodLength` / `periodMonths`, `monthColumnLabels`, `formatPeriod`. No clock:
  "today" is a parameter, as the old fallback year was. 31 tests.
- **`spendingReport.ts`** — `SpendingReport.year` → `period`; `months: number[]` →
  `YearMonth[]`; `ReportRow.ytd` → `total` and `priorYtd` → `priorTotal` (the old
  names lied once the column stopped being year-to-date). `buildSpendingReport`
  takes `(…, period, today)`; `visibleMonths` and `hasReportData` are exported.
  38 tests.
- **`spendingComparison.ts`** — `CompareMode`, `comparisonPeriod`,
  `comparisonModes`, `comparisonLabel`; `withPriorPeriod` made non-mutating. Its
  index/positional matching is otherwise untouched, so a prior report built over a
  shifted period aligns index-for-index. 23 tests.
- **`spendingDrilldown.ts`** — the month column is absolute (`{ year, month }`),
  `ytd` → `total`, and the four context arguments collapse into one
  `DrilldownContext`. The Total column is bounded by the **visible** months (so it
  matches the number clicked), while `periodFrom`/`periodTo` echo the **selected**
  period (so returning restores what was asked for). 14 tests.
- **`PeriodPicker.svelte`** (new, 9 render tests) and the page's compare
  `<select>`; `SpendingChart` takes `periodLabel` / `priorLabel` props instead of
  doing its own `report.year - 1`, keeping period arithmetic out of the chart.
- **`ExpenseService.getExpenseDateBounds()`** (3 tests) for the picker's years.
- **Loading got simpler, not harder:** one fetch over `period start − 12 months →
period end` and three builds off it (current, prior-year, prior-period),
  replacing the two year-sized fetches.
- **Verification:** `npm run verify` clean (check, check:deno, lint, 1456 server
  tests); the browser project passes 150 including the new picker and layout
  specs. Live end-to-end pass by the maintainer, like the earlier slices.

**Date:** 2026-07-09
**Status:** 🚧 **Mostly built.** Every slice described below is live except the
six listed under _Left_.

**Live:** the table view, the chart view, table-cell drill-down into Expenses,
the editable hierarchy (assign a Category to a Grouping, re-parent a Grouping,
add & rename Groupings), assign-on-create, historical-year expense import from
CSV/Excel, and year-over-year comparison (a Change column on the table +
side-by-side prior-year bars on the chart).

**Left**, roughly in order of value:

- **Chart-bar drill-down** — table cells link into `/expenses`; chart bars still
  don't. `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` already exists, so this is wiring.
- **Cumulative pace line** and **diverging change bars** — the two richer YoY
  views ([options 3 and 4](#the-options-cheapest--richest)). Diverging bars are
  also the only remaining way to surface _disappeared_ spend.
- A **multi-chart-type menu**.
- **Export** (CSV / PDF), and **promoting the report to the home page**.

**Period selection** — whole-month periods of up to a year (Jul → Jun), replacing
the calendar-year lock — is **built** ([below](#period-selection--built-)), and
took the hardcoded **"Year to Date"** heading with it. **Quarters are a non-goal**
(a quarter is just a 3-month period the picker expresses).

**Will not be built** — settled, not deferred: **Importance-area CRUD** (the 3
areas are fixed); **Grouping delete and reorder**; and the **Bridge / waterfall**
view, which was built and then **removed as not intuitive**
([ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) — do not
rebuild it).

1	# Spending Report Design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-09
4	**Status:** 🚧 **Mostly built.** Every slice described below is live except the
5	four listed under _Left_.
6	
7	**Live:** the table view, the chart view, table-cell drill-down into Expenses,
8	the editable hierarchy (assign a Category to a Grouping, re-parent a Grouping,
9	add & rename Groupings), assign-on-create, historical-year expense import from
10	CSV/Excel, year-over-year comparison (a Change column on the table +
11	side-by-side prior-year bars on the chart), and selectable whole-month periods.
12	
13	**Left**, roughly in order of value:
14	
15	- **Chart-bar drill-down** — table cells link into `/expenses`; chart bars still
16	  don't. `buildSpendingDrilldownParams` already exists, so this is wiring.
17	- **Cumulative pace line** and **diverging change bars** — the two richer YoY
18	  views ([options 3 and 4](#the-options-cheapest--richest)). Diverging bars are
19	  also the only remaining way to surface _disappeared_ spend.
20	- A **multi-chart-type menu**.
21	- **Export** (CSV / PDF), and **promoting the report to the home page**.
22	
23	**Period selection** — whole-month periods of up to a year (Jul → Jun), replacing
24	the calendar-year lock — is **built** ([below](#period-selection--built-)), and
25	took the hardcoded **"Year to Date"** heading with it. **Quarters are a non-goal**
26	(a quarter is just a 3-month period the picker expresses).
27	
28	**Will not be built** — settled, not deferred: **Importance-area CRUD** (the 3
29	areas are fixed); **Grouping delete and reorder**; and the **Bridge / waterfall**
30	view, which was built and then **removed as not intuitive**
31	([ADR-0004](../adr/0004-abandon-spending-bridge-waterfall-view.md) — do not
32	rebuild it).
33	
34	## Overview
35	
36	A top-level **Spending** report that rolls up Expenses by **Importance →
37	Grouping → Category** across the months of a year. It replaces the Excel pivot
38	table the family currently maintains by hand. ("Spending Report" is the working
39	term; pin the final ubiquitous-language name in `domain-model.md` when built.)
40	
41	Built ✅: the **table view** (v1), the **chart view** (an accordion magnitude bar
42	chart), **cell drill-down** into the Expenses view, and **hierarchy editing**
43	(assign categories to groups, re-parent groups, assign-on-create) — see
44	[Implementation status](#implementation-status),
45	[Spending Chart](#spending-chart-graphical-presentation--built-),
46	[Drill-down](#drill-from-a-table-cell-into-the-expenses-view--built-), and
47	[Editable hierarchy](#editable-hierarchy--assign--re-parent--built-). Year-over-year
48	comparison (a table Change column + chart marker) is also built (see
49	[Year-over-year comparison](#year-over-year-comparison--table-columns--bar-marker-built-)).
50	Still deferred: selectable periods, richer YoY views (pace line / diverging),
51	tier CRUD, and export (see [Deferred](#deferred-later-slices)).
52	
53	## Data model (new)
54	
55	The category hierarchy today is flat: `categories (family_id, name, color)`.
56	There is no Grouping or Importance layer. v1 adds two tiers as real,
57	family-scoped tables so they are first-class and become editable later.
58	
59	- `importance_areas (id, family_id, name, sort_order)` — e.g. Essential
60	  (sort_order 1), Priorities (2), Other (3). The numeric prefix in the sample
61	  (`1. Essential`) becomes `sort_order`, not part of the name.
62	- `category_groups (id, family_id, name, importance_area_id)` — **Importance
63	  attaches to the Grouping**, not to individual categories. Matches the sample
64	  (all of Transportation is Essential) and makes the roll-up a clean two-hop
65	  join. If a future need arises for two categories in one group to have
66	  different importances, revisit — no counterexample in the current sample.
67	- `categories` gains `group_id → category_groups`. A Category belongs to a
68	  Group; the Group carries the Importance.
69	
70	**Seeding.** Derive default Importance areas and Groupings from
71	`docs/SampleHierachy.txt` (cleaned). Map the existing default categories into
72	Groups by name. Near-duplicate categories in the sample (`Car - Insurance` vs
73	`Car insurance`, `Gas` vs `Car - Gas`, `Parking` vs `Car - Parking`) are **not
74	auto-merged** — recognizable names are mapped, the rest fall to Uncategorized.
75	New families are seeded via the same path as `createDefaultCategories`, so any
76	future family gets a working report out of the box.
77	
78	## Report content
79	
80	- **Source:** receipts/Expenses (the app's source of truth for spending), **not**
81	  bank transactions. Bucketed by `transaction_date` (purchase date, not upload
82	  date).

content.text:
Built and staged. **I did not commit** — project CLAUDE.md forbids it ("Never run `git commit`. Only humans commit"), which overrides the skill's instruction.

**Gate status:** `npm run verify` clean (check, check:deno, lint, 1457 server tests). Browser project 150 passed. Production build succeeds when given the `PUBLIC_SUPABASE_*` values — a bare `npm run build` still fails on the missing env vars, which is the documented pre-existing FIFO `.env` behaviour, not this change.

**What shipped**

- **`spendingPeriod.ts`** (replaces `spendingYear.ts`) — `Period`/`YearMonth`, `parsePeriodParams`/`periodParams`, month arithmetic, `monthColumnLabels`, `formatPeriod`. Clock is a parameter, as the old fallback year was. 31 tests.
- **`+page.ts`** — parses `?from=`/`?to=` (legacy `?year=` still works) and `redirect`s anything non-canonical, so URL and picker always agree. There's a test pinning `parsePeriodParams` idempotent over `periodParams` — that property is the only thing stopping the redirect looping.
- **`PeriodPicker.svelte`** — four selects plus the ← → arrows, which now shift by the period's own length. The 12-month cap and the drag-To-with-From rule are structural (the To selects only *list* valid months), so nothing snaps back. Year options come from `ExpenseService.getExpenseDateBounds()`.
- **Comparison** — one dropdown, Off / vs last year / vs previous period, collapsing to one option at 12 months. `withPriorPeriod` is now **non-mutating**: the page derives the rendered report from an un-annotated base, so switching modes can't strand a stale `priorTotal`.
- **Round-trip** — drill-down carries `periodFrom`/`periodTo`; the layout's Spending tab forwards them; the hierarchy editor's link and Back both carry the period too.
- Renames that the period made honest: `ReportRow.ytd` → `total`, `priorYtd` → `priorTotal`, the `ytd` drill-down column → `total`, and the heading → **"Total"** (retiring the "Year to Date" known limitation).

**One deliberate deviation from what we agreed**, now recorded in the doc: columns drop trailing future months only if they're *also empty*. A flat cut at today would have dropped a future-dated receipt — which this app allows and merely flags — out of the grid *and* out of the Grand Total, which is supposed to tie out to real spend.

Two things to know: the design doc's `?year=`-era passages are now marked superseded rather than rewritten, and `version.ts` shows 0.70 in the staged set — that was your edit, not mine.
